for the Bootstrap-style "drop in a URL" experience, and per-component modularization is undercut by the
size of the mandatory token foundation. Two asks:

1. **CSS** — pull an *incremental* subset of components through a single URL (via `@import`/`<link>`),
   with an interactive docs picker that builds the URL — *and* make it actually pay off by shrinking the
   token foundation you must load alongside it.
2. **Web components** — same idea, plus a classic `<script src>` drop-in and true per-component
   cherry-picking.

### What's already true (verified)

- **The token foundation is the real bottleneck.** `@pantoken/css` `dist/style.css` is 1.5 MB raw but
  **137 KB gzip / 107 KB brotli** over the wire (no CDN serves uncompressed). **86% of it (1.36 MB raw)
  is 2,487 `@property` registration blocks**; only 13% is the `:root`/`light-dark()` declarations
  components read via `var()`. Every `@property` block carries a recoverable `initial-value`, so a
  declarations-only "lean" sheet is clean to produce and measures **~25–35 KB gzip** (~5x smaller).
- `toCss(tokens)` (`formats/css/src/to-css.ts`) already splits tokens: **concrete → `@property`**
  (`properties[]`), **contextual (`var()`/`light-dark()`) → `:root` declaration** (`declarations[]` via
  `isContextual`). It takes a `ToCssOptions` ({ scope, plugins }) and composes via `buildCssFile`.
  `formats/css/src/index.ts` exports `css = toCss(tokens)`.
- `@pantoken/components` ships ~46 per-component files (`button.css` ~11 KB, most ~2 KB) plus aggregate
  sheets, all addressable via `"./*.css"`. Component CSS + `icons.css` + the token sheet use only inline
  `data:` URIs — **combine-safe**. `fonts.css` uses relative `../assets/fonts/…` — **NOT** combine-safe.
- A lone component needs the `--instui-*` tokens on the page, plus elevation + focus-outline `:root`
  vars — which today live only in `@pantoken/components` (`components.css` barrel + `base.css`), NOT in
  the token sheet. Those are bespoke TS composites in `formats/components/src/declarations/{elevation,
  focus}.ts`, referencing ingredient tokens that already ship in the token sheet.
- `@pantoken/css` sits **below** `@pantoken/components`; deps `@pantoken/model`, `@pantoken/plugin-kit`,
  `@pantoken/tokens`. Both packages share `@pantoken/tokens`.
- `@pantoken/web-components` is ESM-only, auto-registers all 30 elements, injects a `foundationCss()`
  `:root` block precisely because the token sheet lacks elevation/focus, and has no IIFE build.
  `ElementDefinition` carries `.name`; `DEFINITIONS` is load-bearing order (`date-time-input` →
  `date-input` → `calendar`).
- The docs VitePress site registers one global component (`vitepress-mermaid`) via `enhanceApp`, keeps
  UI strings in `docs/.vitepress/i18n.ts`, hardcodes nav/sidebar per-locale in `config.ts`. Canonical
  component list is `COMPONENTS` in `formats/components/src/components/index.ts` (filter `kind ===
  "component"`); per-component CSS filename = `component.name`.

### Decisions taken (with the user)

- **Keystone — lean token sheet.** Add a declarations-only token entry (~25–35 KB gzip) as the CDN/embed
  foundation; keep the full typed `style.css` as the default for bundler/app consumers. Without this the
  CDN work isn't worth doing; with it, "foundation + one button" is ~Bootstrap-sized.
- **CSS foundation — option 3.** Move elevation + focus-outline vars into the token sheet (both variants)
  so any single component + the lean sheet is self-sufficient. **No `foundation.css`.** `base.css` stays
  an opt-in reset (page-invasive `box-sizing`/`color-scheme` — forcing it would regress embedding).
- **Web components — all three tracks:** document ESM CDN, add an IIFE `<script>` build, add a
  per-component register API.
- **Docs — an interactive `<CdnPicker />`** that builds the combine URL from checkboxes.

---

## Part 0 — Lean token sheet (keystone)

Add a declarations-only variant of the token sheet so CDN consumers load ~25–35 KB gzip instead of 137.
Most of the weight is 1,777 `@property syntax:"<image>"` icon data-URIs (of 2,487 total) — pure ballast
in the CDN case.

**Why this is safe (verified):** no `--instui-*` token is ever animated as a custom property. Every
animation in the repo (badge pulse, focus-outline, spinner, checkbox/radio, popover/tray, img filter, …)
targets a *regular* CSS property (`opacity`, `transform`, `outline-color`, `filter`, …) that reads a
token via `var()` — interpolation happens on the CSS property, not the custom property, so it works
whether or not the token is `@property`-registered. The one directly-animated custom property (`--value`,
progress-circle) is **component-local**: its `@property` ships in `progress-circle.css`, not the token
sheet, so lean doesn't touch it. So the "keep typed" set is **empty today** — but the design stays
selective + guarded because the user wants animations preserved robustly ("there may be others").

Design it selectively, not as a blunt strip:

- **`formats/css/src/to-css.ts`** — add `lean?: boolean` (default `false`) and `keepTyped?: (name:
  string) => boolean` (default `() => false`) to `ToCssOptions`. In lean mode, route every concrete token
  to `declarations[]` (plain `:root { --x: value }`) **except** those matching `keepTyped`, which stay as
  typed `@property` registrations. The concrete values (today only in `@property { initial-value }`) are
  thereby preserved as ordinary declarations. Update the doc comment/marker.
- **Plugins in scope + latent-bug fix** — `appendContribution` currently emits plugin `c.properties` as
  `@property` blocks with a hardcoded `inherits: true` and **no `isContextual` guard** (a real bug: a
  plugin passing a `var()`/`light-dark()` initial-value emits invalid `@property`). Fix it and route it
  through the same policy: (a) always send a contextual initial-value to a declaration (guard fix,
  applies in both modes); (b) in lean mode, flatten non-`keepTyped` `c.properties` to `:root`
  declarations too. No shipped plugin sets `c.properties` and the default sheet passes no plugins, so
  this is a no-op today for our output — it's correctness + future-proofing (e.g. astro's `pantokenCss`
  forwards caller plugins).
- **`formats/css/src/index.ts`** — add `export const leanCss = toCss(tokens, { lean: true });` alongside
  the typed `css` (Part A's foundation plugin is passed to both).
- **`formats/css/scripts/generate.ts`** — also write `generated/style.lean.css` from `leanCss`.
- **`formats/css/vite.config.ts`** — add a `style.lean` pack entry → `generated/style.lean.css`.
- **`formats/css/package.json`** — add `"./style.lean.css": "./dist/style.lean.css"` to `exports`.
- **Guard test (protects "there may be others"):** a repo-level check that scans `formats/components` +
  `renderers/web-components` CSS for custom properties that are transitioned/animated directly or
  interpolated in `@keyframes`, resolves which are `--instui-*` tokens present in the token sheet, and
  fails if any such token is NOT in `keepTyped` (i.e. would be flattened). Seeds `keepTyped` from this —
  empty today, self-correcting if a future component animates a token property.
- **Lean-sheet test:** assert `style.lean.css` has zero `@property` (given empty `keepTyped`), carries
  representative concrete tokens + the elevation/focus vars as `:root` declarations, and is materially
  smaller than `style.css`.

Tradeoff (document): the lean sheet drops typed custom properties — `syntax` validation, guaranteed
`initial-value` fallbacks, and typed interpretation inside `calc()`/`conic-gradient`/color functions.
That's a *visual-parity* risk, not an animation risk — covered by the render-diff in Verification.

---

## Part A — Move elevation + focus-outline into the token sheet

Chosen depth: **light** — relocate the two pure `[name,value][]` builders down one layer and emit them
from `@pantoken/css`; leave the cssdoc `@declaration` records in `@pantoken/components`. (The "deep"
alternative — first-class IR `Token`s — is a larger model change; note as future, don't do now.)

### A1. Relocate the pure builders to `@pantoken/utils`
Move `elevationDeclarations`, `focusOutlineDeclarations`, `focusOutlineRules`, `FOCUSABLE_SELECTOR`, and
constants (`ELEVATION_GEOMETRY`/`ELEVATION_ALIASES`/`ELEVATION_NAMES`) from
`formats/components/src/declarations/{elevation,focus}.ts` into `@pantoken/utils`
(`packages/utils/src/declarations.ts`, new; re-exported from the `src/index.ts` barrel). `@pantoken/utils`
depends only on `@pantoken/model` + arkregex, so it's a safe low-level home with no cycle (`css` and
`components` both sit above it). **Promote `@pantoken/utils` from a devDependency to a runtime dependency
in `formats/css/package.json`** so `@pantoken/css` can import the builders; `@pantoken/components` keeps
it as a devDep (its CSS is emitted by build scripts). Keep the builders pure (`[name,value][]`) — no
Node imports (they're safe for the browser-facing graphs), and no cssdoc/`Definition` concerns move.

### A2. Emit them from `@pantoken/css` (into both sheets)
In `formats/css/src/index.ts`, feed the elevation + focus-outline declarations into `toCss` — cleanest
via a small foundation plugin (`ToCssOptions.plugins`, `css` hook `declarations`) or an extra section.
Because the values are contextual (`var(...)`), `isContextual()` routes them to `:root` declarations in
**both** the typed `css` and the lean `leanCss` builds — so both sheets carry `--instui-elevation-*` (8)
and `--instui-focus-outline-*` (11). Every ingredient token they reference already ships, so no dangling
refs.

### A3. Stop double-emitting in `@pantoken/components`
- `componentsCss()` (`formats/components/src/index.ts`) — drop the leading `elevationCss()` block (token
  sheet owns it now); components keep referencing `var(--instui-elevation-*)`.
- `baseCss()` — change the appended `focusOutlineCss()` to **`focusOutlineRules()` only** (keep the
  `:focus-visible` ring behavior; the var defs are now in the token sheet).
- Re-export the moved builders from `@pantoken/components` so existing importers + the public-surface
  test keep working; `elevationCss()`/`focusOutlineCss()` (doc-wrapped) and the cssdoc
  `elevation`/`focus` `Definition`s stay here, importing the moved pure builders.

### A4. Retire the web-components foundation injection
`renderers/web-components/src/index.ts` — remove `foundationCss()` and the `<style
id="pantoken-foundation">` injection in `register()` (redundant now the required token sheet carries
them); update the module JSDoc; drop the `foundationCss` export (`@alpha`, fine).

### A5. Keep other consumers working
`renderers/pendo/src/build.ts` (self-contained sheet) still imports `elevationCss`/`focusOutlineRules`/
`focusOutlineDeclarations` — available via the components re-exports; no change.
`docs/scripts/stage-component-assets.ts` (`focusOutlineCss`) and
`formats/components/scripts/generate.ts` (`ELEVATION_NAMES`) — unaffected via re-exports.

### A6. Tests
Update `formats/components/tests/sheets.test.ts` (`components.css` no longer leads with elevation
`:root`; `base.css` no longer defines `--instui-focus-outline-*`, only ring rules). Adjust IR-drift so
`@pantoken/css` **expects** the elevation/focus vars. Add a `@pantoken/css` test asserting both sheets
contain them. `public-surface.test.ts` passes via re-exports.

**Result — the CDN combine URL (foundation = lean sheet):**
```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/combine/npm/@pantoken/css@0/style.lean.css,npm/@pantoken/components@0/button.css,npm/@pantoken/components@0/badge.css">
```
`base.css` (reset) optional; `fonts.css` always a separate plain `<link>`.

---

## Part B — Web components

- **B1. Document ESM CDN (no code):** `<script type="module">import
  "https://esm.sh/@pantoken/web-components";</script>` auto-registers all elements; needs the token-sheet
  `<link>` (lean is fine).
- **B2. IIFE `<script>` build:** add `renderers/web-components/scripts/build-iife.ts` — a direct-`node`
  script (call Vite's `build()` API directly per the vp-nested-spawn constraint; no `vp`/`pnpm` shell-out)
  emitting `dist/web-components.iife.js`: format `iife`, global `PantokenWebComponents` (exposing
  `register`), no externals (inline `@pantoken/components`/`@pantoken/icons`); bottom-of-file `register()`
  auto-registers at load. Wire into the `build` task in `renderers/web-components/vite.config.ts` after
  `vp pack`. First check whether `vp pack` can emit `iife` + `globalName` directly (prefer that; script is
  the fallback).
- **B3. Per-component register API:** extend `register(target, options)` with `only?: readonly string[]`
  (base names). Build `ctx` as today, then iterate `DEFINITIONS` in canonical order defining only names in
  the expanded set. Add a `NESTED_DEPS` map so composites pull children (`date-time-input` → `date-input`
  → `calendar`); verify the full map by auditing which `src/elements/*.ts` render nested `tag(...)`
  elements. Keep the all-elements auto-`register()` as default (back-compat). Note `esm.sh?exports=` can't
  cherry-pick (registration is a runtime side effect, not tree-shakeable).

---

## Part C — Docs: CDN guide + interactive `<CdnPicker />`

### C1. The picker component
`docs/.vitepress/theme/components/CdnPicker.vue` — Vue 3 `<script setup lang="ts">`, `<style scoped>`
keyed to `--vp-*` (match `ThemeSelector.vue`). Name must not start with `instui-`.
- Checkbox list of components → live-builds a jsDelivr combine URL: base
  `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/combine/` + `npm/@pantoken/css@<v>/style.lean.css` + one
  `npm/@pantoken/components@<v>/<name>.css` per checked box. Toggles: `<link>` vs `@import`; optional
  `base.css` (reset); lean vs full token sheet (default lean, with the size delta shown); a note that
  fonts load separately. A "Copy" button.
- Optional second mode (ties to B3): a web-components tab emitting a `register(customElements, { only:
  [...] })` snippet + import-map for the checked elements — include if low-cost; CSS URL is primary.
- **Component list — do not hardcode.** Add a `docs/scripts/*.ts` node that imports `COMPONENTS` from
  `formats/components/src/components/index.ts`, filters `kind === "component"`, maps to `.name`, captures
  the current `@pantoken/components`/`@pantoken/css` versions, and writes a manifest under
  `docs/.vitepress/theme/generated/` (mirroring existing generated docs artifacts). The picker imports
  it. Wire the script into the docs generate step.
- **i18n:** route the picker's UI labels through `docs/.vitepress/i18n.ts` + `themeConfig`, read via
  `useData().theme` with English defaults (the `ThemeSelector`/`themeSelector` precedent). Component
  names aren't translated.

### C2. Registration + guide page
- Register `<CdnPicker />` globally in `docs/.vitepress/theme/index.ts` `enhanceApp` (like
  `vitepress-mermaid`).
- New guide `docs/guide/cdn.md` (+ mirrored `docs/hu/guide/cdn.md`; parity via
  `docs/scripts/check-locale-parity.ts`) embedding `<CdnPicker />`, documenting: the lean vs full token
  sheet (with the 137 KB → ~30 KB gzip story and the typed-property tradeoff), cherry-pick combine, the
  barrel, fonts-as-separate-`<link>`, ordering (token sheet → optional base → components), the ESM
  import, the IIFE `<script>`, and `register({ only })`. State the non-goal: a literal `?components=…`
  query param isn't off-the-shelf (combine is the closest; a true builder would be a separate edge worker).
- Add the sidebar label key to both locale blocks in `i18n.ts` and a sidebar entry (Guides) in
  `config.ts`. Add a short pointer from `README.md`.

---

## Files to modify (representative)

- **Lean sheet:** `formats/css/src/to-css.ts` (lean/keepTyped + `appendContribution` `isContextual`
  guard fix), `formats/css/src/index.ts`, `formats/css/scripts/generate.ts`, `formats/css/vite.config.ts`,
  `formats/css/package.json`, + a `@pantoken/css` lean-sheet test + a repo-level animated-custom-property
  guard check.
- **Foundation move:** `packages/utils/src/declarations.ts` (new) + `packages/utils/src/index.ts` ← from
  `formats/components/src/declarations/{elevation,focus}.ts`; `formats/css/package.json` (promote `utils`
  devDep → dep); `formats/css/src/index.ts` (import builders from `@pantoken/utils` + emit);
  `formats/components/src/index.ts` + `src/declarations/{elevation,focus,index}.ts` (de-dupe + re-export).
- **Web components:** `renderers/web-components/src/index.ts`; `renderers/web-components/scripts/build-iife.ts`
  (new) + `renderers/web-components/vite.config.ts`.
- **Docs:** `docs/.vitepress/theme/components/CdnPicker.vue` (new), `docs/.vitepress/theme/index.ts`,
  `docs/.vitepress/i18n.ts`, `docs/.vitepress/config.ts`, `docs/scripts/<manifest>.ts` (new),
  `docs/guide/cdn.md` + `docs/hu/guide/cdn.md`, `README.md`.
- **Tests:** `formats/components/tests/sheets.test.ts` (+ new `@pantoken/css` test).

## Verification

1. `vp run build` for `@pantoken/utils`, `@pantoken/css`, `@pantoken/components`,
   `@pantoken/web-components`.
2. **Lean sheet:** confirm `formats/css/dist/style.lean.css` has zero `@property`, carries the concrete
   tokens as `:root` declarations plus elevation/focus vars, and gzips to roughly the ~25–35 KB band
   (`gzip -9 -c dist/style.lean.css | wc -c`). Confirm the typed `style.css` still has `@property` blocks
   and also carries elevation/focus.
3. **Foundation resolves standalone + visual parity:** serve `formats/css/dist` + `formats/components/dist`
   on a throwaway static server (own port, `--strictPort`); scratch page linking `style.lean.css` + a
   couple of component files; via preview tools verify `.instui-button`/`.instui-badge` render with
   correct color, **shadow**, and **focus ring** — no `base.css`, no barrel, no typed sheet. Then
   **render-diff lean vs typed:** load the same components once under `style.lean.css` and once under
   `style.css` and screenshot-compare, exercising the `@property`-sensitive cases (icon `<image>` tokens
   via `background`/`mask`, `calc()`/`conic-gradient` usages like progress-circle, badge pulse
   mid-animation) to confirm the flatten introduces no visual regression.
4. **Per-component register:** scratch page, `register(customElements, { only: ["date-time-input"] })`;
   assert `instui-date-time-input`/`instui-date-input`/`instui-calendar` defined, `instui-drilldown` not.
5. **IIFE:** scratch page `<script src>` to the IIFE + token-sheet `<link>`; global present,
   `<instui-button>` upgrades and renders (shadows/focus intact — proves the token sheet supplies them).
6. **Docs picker:** `vp run docs:dev` (own port), open `/guide/cdn`, toggle boxes/lean-vs-full, confirm
   the URL updates and Copy works; open the URL's constituent files via the local server to confirm they
   resolve; verify the `hu` page renders translated chrome.
7. `pnpm run ready` + `pnpm run check:publish` (via `vp`) — exports, types, locale parity, publish gates.

## Risks / caveats

- jsDelivr combine has historically mishandled relative `url()` and returned wrong `Content-Type` on
  combined CSS. Our component + token CSS is `data:`-URI-only (verified) — keep `fonts.css` out of every
  combine URL; note the content-type caveat in the guide.
- **Lean-sheet tradeoff:** dropping `@property` removes typed-property *interpretation* (validation,
  `initial-value` fallbacks, typed values inside `calc()`/`conic-gradient`/color functions). Animation is
  **not** at risk — verified that no `--instui-*` token is animated as a custom property, and the one
  animated custom property (`--value`) is component-local. Residual risk is visual parity, caught by the
  render-diff (Verification 3). The `keepTyped` set + guard test protect any future token animation. Keep
  the typed `style.css` as the recommended default for bundler consumers.
- Moving the builders into `@pantoken/utils` promotes it from a devDep to a runtime dep of `@pantoken/css`
  (`packages/utils` depends only on `@pantoken/model` + arkregex, so no cycle, a tiny runtime-graph
  addition). The builders are pure string functions (no Node imports), so the browser-facing
  `@pantoken/components`/`@pantoken/web-components` graphs stay Node-free per CLAUDE.md.
- Removing the web-components foundation injection makes the token sheet a hard runtime requirement for
  shadows/focus (already was for other tokens) — call out in the web-components docs.
- The IIFE bundles both `@pantoken/*` deps → larger than ESM; document as a convenience target.
- A literal `?components=…` query-param builder is out of scope; a future edge-worker project if wanted.

## The lean-flatten premise was wrong

I built the `@property`-flatten lean mode and measured the real output. It barely helps:

| sheet | raw | **gzip** | brotli |
|---|---|---|---|

Flattening `@property` → declarations saves **~2 KB gzip**, not the ~110 KB I'd projected. My earlier "~24 KB" estimate was a measurement bug — the data-URI values contain `;`, and my regex truncated them, so the fake lean sheet looked tiny. The `@property` boilerplate is highly repetitive and gzip erases it either way.

## Where the weight actually is

**1,777 `--instui-icon-*` data-URI tokens = 1.31 MB of the 1.64 MB raw.** The token sheet embeds the *entire* icon set as CSS custom properties. Strip the icons and the foundation is **raw 324 KB → gzip ~23 KB** — the real ~6x win.

Components reference only **11 distinct icons** (`check`, `chevron-down/right/up`, `circle-alert/check/x`, `info`, `minus`, `triangle-alert`, `x`), consumed as inlineable `url(data:...)` masks (e.g. `mask: var(--instui-icon-x)`). The other ~1,766 belong to the opt-in `icons.css` glyph sheet.

## What still stands vs. what changes

Most of the work is unaffected and correct: moving the builders to `@pantoken/utils`, emitting elevation/focus into the token sheet, the components de-dupe, and the `appendContribution` bug fix. **Only the "how do we shrink the foundation" lever changes** — from "flatten `@property`" (drop it; ~2 KB, not worth the typed-property tradeoff) to "**exclude the full icon set**." That raises one real decision: components need those 11 icons, so where do they come from?

18:export interface Definition {

=== getting-started.md head ===
# Getting started

pantoken takes Instructure UI's design tokens and icons, resolves them once, and reshapes that one
model into packages for many platforms: plain stylesheets, SCSS and Less, React and Vue and Svelte,
Tailwind and Panda, native Swift and Kotlin, WordPress and Drupal, Figma, and more.

You install the smallest package that fits your task. Everything is also re-exported by the unified
`pantoken` package, so you can start there and narrow down later.

## The token model

Tokens are CSS custom properties named `--instui-<group>-<name>`, for example
`--instui-color-background-brand` or `--instui-spacing-space-md`. Three themes ship: `rebrand`
(the default, with `light-dark()` where light and dark differ), `canvas`, and `canvasHighContrast`.
Icons are `<image>` tokens (`--instui-icon-<name>`) derived from Lucide plus Instructure's custom
glyphs.

## Style a web app

Install the stylesheet and import it once. It defines every `--instui-*` property, so you reference
them straight from your own CSS.

```sh
npm i @pantoken/css
```

```ts
import "@pantoken/css/inject";
```

input.content:
# CDN & distribution

pantoken publishes every package to npm, so you can pull tokens, components, and web components straight
from a CDN — no build step, no bundler. This page covers the CSS combine URL (with an interactive
builder), plus the web-component drop-ins.

## The token foundation

Every pantoken component reads `--instui-*` custom properties from a token sheet on the page. Two
variants ship:

- `@pantoken/css/style.lean.css` — the recommended CDN foundation. It carries every token except the
  full icon set, so it's about 23 KB gzipped.
- `@pantoken/css/style.css` — the full sheet, including all ~1,777 icon glyph tokens
  (`--instui-icon-*`). About 140 KB gzipped. Load this if you reference icons broadly via
  `var(--instui-icon-*)`.

The elevation scale and focus-ring variables ride in both sheets, so shadows and the focus ring work with
just the foundation loaded.

## Pick your components

jsDelivr's combine endpoint pulls the token foundation plus only the component stylesheets you need, in a
single request. Check the components you want, and the builder writes the URL:

<CdnPicker />

Each component file is small — most are around 2 KB. A component that renders icons (`alert`, `checkbox`,
and a few others) needs those glyphs, so the builder adds `@pantoken/components/component-icons.css` (about
0.5 KB gzipped — the 11 icons the component set uses) whenever you pick the lean sheet. The full sheet
already carries them.

### Load order and fonts

Load the token foundation first, then the optional base reset, then the component files. The combine URL
above already orders them for you. Fonts are the one exception: `@pantoken/components/fonts.css` points at
font files by relative path, so combine can't rewrite them — load it as its own `<link>`:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/components/fonts.css">
```

### Everything at once

To pull the whole component library instead of cherry-picking, point at the barrel (about 141 KB gzipped)
alongside the token sheet:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/combine/npm/@pantoken/css/style.css,npm/@pantoken/components/components.css">
```

## Web components

`@pantoken/web-components` registers framework-agnostic `<instui-*>` custom elements. They inline their
own CSS, but still read tokens from a sheet on the page, so load a token foundation too.

### ES modules (recommended)

An ESM CDN resolves the package's dependencies for you. This registers every element:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/css/style.css">
<script type="module">import "https://esm.sh/@pantoken/web-components";</script>
```

Use the full token sheet (or the lean sheet plus `component-icons.css`) so icon-rendering elements like
`<instui-alert>` resolve their glyphs.

To register just some elements — and their nested dependencies — import `register` and pass `only`:

```html
<script type="module">
  import { register } from "https://esm.sh/@pantoken/web-components";
  // Pulls in date-input and calendar automatically.
  register(customElements, { only: ["date-time-input"] });
</script>
```

### A classic script tag

For a no-modules drop-in, load the IIFE build. It bundles its dependencies and auto-registers every
element on load, exposing a `PantokenWebComponents` global:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/css/style.css">
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/web-components/dist/web-components.iife.js"></script>
```

It's larger than the ESM path — it inlines `@pantoken/components` and `@pantoken/icons` — so reach for it
only when you can't use modules.

## Pinning versions

The URLs above float to the latest release. Pin a major (or exact) version for production — for example
`@pantoken/css@0` — so an upgrade never surprises you. The picker pins the current published version for
you.

## What's not here

There's no `?components=button,badge` query parameter: no public CDN assembles a bundle from query params.
The combine URL is the closest equivalent, and the picker writes it for you.

# CDN és terjesztés

A pantoken minden csomagot közzétesz az npm-en, így a tokeneket, komponenseket és web-komponenseket
közvetlenül egy CDN-ről is behúzhatod — build lépés és bundler nélkül. Ez az oldal a CSS combine URL-t
(interaktív építővel) és a web-komponens beillesztéseket mutatja be.

## A token alap

Minden pantoken komponens `--instui-*` egyedi tulajdonságokat olvas be egy token lapból az oldalon. Két
változat érhető el:

- `@pantoken/css/style.lean.css` — az ajánlott CDN alap. Minden tokent tartalmaz a teljes ikonkészlet
  kivételével, így körülbelül 23 KB gzip-elve.
- `@pantoken/css/style.css` — a teljes lap, benne mind a ~1777 ikon glyph tokennel
  (`--instui-icon-*`). Körülbelül 140 KB gzip-elve. Ezt töltsd be, ha széles körben hivatkozol ikonokra a
  `var(--instui-icon-*)` segítségével.

Az elevation skála és a fókuszgyűrű változói mindkét lapban benne vannak, így az árnyékok és a
fókuszgyűrű már önmagában az alappal is működnek.

## Válaszd ki a komponenseket

A jsDelivr combine végpontja egyetlen kérésben húzza be a token alapot és csak a szükséges komponens
stíluslapokat. Jelöld be a kívánt komponenseket, és az építő megírja az URL-t:

<CdnPicker />

Minden komponensfájl kicsi — a legtöbb körülbelül 2 KB. Az ikonokat megjelenítő komponensek (`alert`,
`checkbox` és néhány másik) igénylik ezeket a glyph-eket, ezért az építő hozzáadja a
`@pantoken/components/component-icons.css` fájlt (körülbelül 0,5 KB gzip-elve — a komponenskészlet által
használt 11 ikon), amikor a karcsú lapot választod. A teljes lap már tartalmazza őket.

### Betöltési sorrend és betűtípusok

Először a token alapot töltsd be, majd az opcionális alap resetet, végül a komponensfájlokat. A fenti
combine URL már ilyen sorrendben rakja őket. A betűtípusok az egyetlen kivétel: a
`@pantoken/components/fonts.css` relatív útvonalon hivatkozik a betűfájlokra, így a combine nem tudja
átírni őket — töltsd be saját `<link>` elemként:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/components/fonts.css">
```

### Minden egyszerre

Ha a teljes komponenskönyvtárat szeretnéd behúzni válogatás helyett, mutass a gyűjtőlapra (körülbelül
141 KB gzip-elve) a token lap mellett:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/combine/npm/@pantoken/css/style.css,npm/@pantoken/components/components.css">
```

## Web-komponensek

A `@pantoken/web-components` keretrendszer-független `<instui-*>` egyedi elemeket regisztrál. Saját
CSS-üket beágyazzák, de a tokeneket továbbra is az oldalon lévő lapból olvassák, ezért egy token alapot is
tölts be.

### ES modulok (ajánlott)

Egy ESM CDN feloldja helyetted a csomag függőségeit. Ez minden elemet regisztrál:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/css/style.css">
<script type="module">import "https://esm.sh/@pantoken/web-components";</script>
```

Használd a teljes token lapot (vagy a karcsú lapot a `component-icons.css`-szel), hogy az ikonokat
megjelenítő elemek, például az `<instui-alert>`, feloldják a glyph-jeiket.

Ha csak néhány elemet szeretnél regisztrálni — a beágyazott függőségeikkel együtt —, importáld a
`register` függvényt, és add meg az `only` opciót:

```html
<script type="module">
  import { register } from "https://esm.sh/@pantoken/web-components";
  // A date-input és a calendar automatikusan bekerül.
  register(customElements, { only: ["date-time-input"] });
</script>
```

### Klasszikus script tag

Modulok nélküli beillesztéshez töltsd be az IIFE buildet. Ez beágyazza a függőségeit, betöltéskor minden
elemet automatikusan regisztrál, és egy `PantokenWebComponents` globális objektumot tesz elérhetővé:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/css/style.css">
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/web-components/dist/web-components.iife.js"></script>
```

Nagyobb, mint az ESM út — beágyazza a `@pantoken/components` és a `@pantoken/icons` csomagokat —, ezért
csak akkor nyúlj hozzá, ha nem tudsz modulokat használni.

## Verziók rögzítése

A fenti URL-ek a legfrissebb kiadásra mutatnak. Éles környezetben rögzíts egy fő (vagy pontos) verziót —
például `@pantoken/css@0` —, hogy egy frissítés soha ne érjen váratlanul. Az építő helyetted rögzíti az
aktuálisan közzétett verziót.

## Ami nincs itt

Nincs `?components=button,badge` lekérdezési paraméter: egyetlen nyilvános CDN sem állít össze bundle-t
lekérdezési paraméterekből. A combine URL a legközelebbi megfelelő, és az építő megírja helyetted.

**The keystone (Part 0 + A) — a lean token foundation.** Mid-implementation I measured the actual output and found the approved premise was wrong: flattening `@property` saved only ~2 KB gzip (the boilerplate compresses to nothing). - `@pantoken/components/component-icons.css` — the **11 icons** components actually use (549 bytes gzip), auto-detected at build. Picking an icon-using component adds it to the combine URL against the lean sheet.

# CDN & distribution for pantoken CSS and web components

> **Status: implemented and verified.** This file reflects what was actually built. The keystone changed
> during implementation — see "Keystone correction" below — from flattening `@property` to excluding the
> icon set, after measuring that flattening saved only ~2 KB gzip.

## Context

pantoken ships small, individually-publishable packages, but there was no CDN story for the
Bootstrap-style "drop in a URL" experience, and per-component modularization was undercut by the size of
the mandatory token foundation. Two asks:

1. **CSS** — pull an incremental subset of components through one URL (via `@import`/`<link>`), with an
   interactive docs picker — and make it pay off by shrinking the token foundation loaded alongside it.
2. **Web components** — same idea, plus a classic `<script src>` drop-in and true per-component
   cherry-picking.

## Keystone correction (measured during implementation)

The approved plan assumed the token sheet's bulk was `@property` typing boilerplate, so a
declaration-only "lean" sheet would drop it from ~137 KB to ~25 KB gzip. **That was wrong.** Measuring the
real output:

- Flattening `@property` → `:root` declarations saved only **~2 KB gzip** (141 → 139). The boilerplate is
  highly repetitive and gzip erases it either way. (The earlier ~24 KB estimate was a measurement bug: the
  data-URI values contain `;`, and the estimating regex truncated them.)
- **86% of the sheet (1.31 MB raw of 1.64 MB) is the 1,777 `--instui-icon-*` data-URI tokens.** Excluding
  the full icon set drops the foundation to **294 KB raw → 22.5 KB gzip / 17.4 KB brotli** — the real ~6×
  win, with `@property` typing kept intact (so no typed-property/visual-parity tradeoff).
- Components reference only **11 distinct icons** (`check`, `chevron-*`, `circle-*`, `info`, `minus`,
  `triangle-alert`, `x`), consumed as `url(data:…)` masks.

Decision taken (with the user): the lean sheet **omits the full icon set**; the ~11 component-referenced
icons ship separately as `@pantoken/components/component-icons.css`. The `@property`-flatten machinery was
dropped; only the `appendContribution` guard fix (below) was kept.

---

## Part 0 — Lean token sheet + icon split (keystone)

- **`formats/css/src/index.ts`** — `export const leanCss = toCss(tokens.filter(t => !t.name
  .startsWith("--instui-icon-")), { plugins: [foundationPlugin] })`, alongside the full `css`. Icon
  exclusion is a plain token filter — no `toCss` API change needed for it.
- **`formats/css/src/to-css.ts`** — kept the guard fix only: `appendContribution` now routes any
  plugin-contributed property whose initial-value is contextual (`var()`/`light-dark()`) to a `:root`
  declaration instead of emitting an invalid `@property`. (No `lean`/`keepTyped` options — those were part
  of the abandoned flatten approach.)
- **`formats/css/scripts/generate.ts`** — writes `generated/style.lean.css` next to `style.css`.
- **`formats/css/vite.config.ts`** — `style.lean` pack entry.
- **`formats/css/package.json`** — `"./style.lean.css"` export.
- **Tests** (`formats/css/tests/to-css.test.ts`): `leanCss` has no `--instui-icon-`, keeps
  elevation/focus, is < half the size, and is self-contained (no dangling refs); plus the guard-fix test.

## Part A — Move elevation + focus-outline into the token sheet

### A1. Relocate the pure builders to `@pantoken/utils`
`elevationDeclarations`, `focusOutlineDeclarations`, `focusOutlineRules`, `FOCUSABLE_SELECTOR`, and the
elevation constants moved from `formats/components/src/declarations/{elevation,focus}.ts` into
`packages/utils/src/declarations.ts` (re-exported from the utils barrel). `@pantoken/utils` depends only
on `@pantoken/model` + arkregex — no cycle. **Promoted `@pantoken/utils` from devDep → runtime dep in
BOTH `formats/css/package.json` and `formats/components/package.json`** (deviation from the plan's "keep
components on devDep": the published `@pantoken/components` barrel's `componentsCss()` calls the builders
at runtime, so they're a genuine runtime dep). The builders are pure, Node-free string functions.

### A2. Emit them from `@pantoken/css`
A `definePlugin` foundation plugin appends elevation (8) + focus-outline (11) declarations. Values are
contextual, so they land as `:root` declarations in **both** `css` and `leanCss`.

### A3. De-dupe in `@pantoken/components` + emit `component-icons.css`
- `componentsCss()` no longer leads with `elevationCss()`; `baseCss()` emits `focusOutlineRules()` only
  (the ring rules stay; the vars now come from the token sheet). Both keep *referencing* the vars.
- The moved builders are re-exported from the components barrel + declaration files (so `elevationCss`/
  `focusOutlineCss`, the cssdoc `Definition`s, pendo, and `scripts/generate.ts` keep working unchanged).
- **`formats/components/scripts/generate.ts`** emits `generated/component-icons.css`: the `--instui-icon-*`
  glyph tokens the component sheets reference (auto-detected via `var(--instui-icon-…)`, valued from the
  token IR — throws if one is missing). Registered as an aggregate in `vite.config.ts` + a
  `"./component-icons.css"` export. Result: 11 icons, ~549 bytes gzip.

### A4. Retire the web-components foundation injection
`renderers/web-components/src/index.ts` — removed `foundationCss()` + the `<style id=pantoken-foundation>`
injection in `register()` (redundant now the required token sheet carries them); updated the module JSDoc
to note lean-sheet users pair with `component-icons.css`.

### A6. Tests
`formats/components/tests/{sheets,rules/base}.test.ts` updated: components.css no longer defines the
elevation `:root` block; base.css references but no longer defines `--instui-focus-outline-*`; the
IR-drift filter comment updated. Added an **icon-completeness guard** (replaces the plan's now-moot
"animated custom-property guard", since flatten was dropped): every `--instui-icon-*` a component
references must exist in the token IR, so `component-icons.css` fully backs the lean foundation.

`component-icons.css` is added only when a chosen component uses icons and the lean sheet is selected;
`base.css` is optional; `fonts.css` always a separate plain `<link>` (relative `url()`, not combine-safe).

- **B1** — Documented the ESM CDN path (esm.sh / `+esm`), auto-registers all elements.
- **B2** — `renderers/web-components/scripts/build-iife.ts` (direct Vite `build()` call, no nested `vp`)
  emits `dist/web-components.iife.js`: IIFE, `PantokenWebComponents` global, deps inlined, auto-registers
  on load. Wired into the build task after `vp pack`. ~210 KB gzip (inlines the token IR via
  `@pantoken/components`) — a documented convenience target, not the default.

  `NESTED_DEPS` map (`date-time-input → date-input → calendar`). Auto-`register()` (all) stays the
  default. Tests cover the subset + transitive expansion.

- **`docs/scripts/cdn-manifest.ts`** (wired into `docs:assets`) emits
  `.vitepress/theme/generated/cdn-manifest.json` from the `COMPONENTS` registry: shippable component names
  (`kind: "component"`), per-component `needsIcons`, and the current `@pantoken/components`/`@pantoken/css`
  versions.
- **`docs/.vitepress/theme/components/CdnPicker.vue`** (+ `theme/cdn.ts` defaults) — registered globally
  in `enhanceApp`. Builds the combine URL live from checkboxes: lean/full token sheet, `<link>`/`@import`,
  optional base reset, auto-added `component-icons.css`, Copy button, pinned versions. Labels routed
  through `i18n.ts` → `themeConfig.cdnPicker` (English + Hungarian).
- **`docs/guide/cdn.md`** (+ `docs/hu/guide/cdn.md`) embedding `<CdnPicker />`; sidebar entry
  (`sidebar.cdn`) in `i18n.ts` + `config.ts`; README pointer.

1. `vp run ready:all` + `vp run gate:publish` — build, tests, lint, typecheck, export resolution: green.
2. Lean sheet: `dist/style.lean.css` = 294 KB raw / **22.5 KB gzip**, zero `--instui-icon-`, elevation +
   focus present. `component-icons.css` = 11 icons / 549 bytes gzip.
3. Standalone render (static server over the dist files): an `.instui-alert` renders with correct colors,
   **elevation box-shadow**, and its **icon glyph** against only `style.lean.css` + `component-icons.css`
   + `alert.css` — no barrel, no full icon set. (Screenshot captured.)
4. Per-component register: unit tests — `only` subset + `date-time-input` pulling in `date-input` +
   `calendar`, in canonical order.
5. IIFE built; valid IIFE, `PantokenWebComponents` global, no bare imports.
6. Docs picker (vitepress dev): builds correct pinned URLs; lean/full toggle adds/drops
   `component-icons.css`; `<link>`/`@import` switch; i18n renders.

## Deviations from the approved plan

- **Keystone**: icon-exclusion, not `@property`-flatten (measured; flatten ≈ 2 KB, icons ≈ 118 KB gzip).
- `@pantoken/utils` promoted to a runtime dep of `@pantoken/components` too (barrel imports it at runtime).
- Guard test is icon-completeness, not animation (flatten dropped → no animation risk).
- IIFE is ~210 KB gzip (bundles the token IR) — documented convenience target.

- jsDelivr combine mishandles relative `url()` — keep `fonts.css` out of combine (verified everything else
  is `data:`-URI only).
- The lean sheet drops the full `var(--instui-icon-*)` set; consumers using icons broadly load the full
  token sheet (or `icons.css`).
- No `?components=…` query-param builder — the combine URL is the closest off-the-shelf equivalent.

name: Deploy docs

# Build the VitePress + TypeDoc site and publish it to GitHub Pages.
# Enable Pages first: repo Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source = GitHub Actions.
#
# Gated behind CI: this runs after the CI workflow finishes on main and only deploys when CI passed,
# reusing the packages CI already built (downloaded as an artifact) instead of rebuilding the
# workspace. `workflow_dispatch` is the manual escape hatch — it builds the assets fresh (for a
# `[skip ci]` commit, or to re-run a failed deploy), since the CI artifact won't exist for it.

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ["CI"]
    types: [completed]
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  actions: read # download the build-output artifact from the triggering CI run
  pages: write
  id-token: write

# Let a running deploy finish; don't cancel it mid-publish.
concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  # Deploy only after a successful CI run (or a manual dispatch), and — for a CI-triggered run — only
  # when the pushed commit actually changed something the site renders.
  changes:
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      should_deploy: ${{ steps.decide.outputs.should_deploy }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha || github.ref }}
          fetch-depth: 2
      - name: Decide whether to deploy
        id: decide
        shell: bash
        run: |
          if [[ "${{ github.event_name }}" == "workflow_dispatch" ]]; then
            echo "should_deploy=true" >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"
            exit 0
          fi

content.text:
Fixed. **[PR #14 — fix(docs): commit hu translation cache](https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken/pull/14)** on `fix/docs-locale-cache`.

## What went wrong

The docs deploy failure wasn't the build — it was `check-locale-drift`. The site's Hungarian pages are machine-translated from a committed cache (`docs/i18n-cache/`), and that check fails if any current English block lacks a cache entry. The CDN work added new English prose (the `cdn.md` guide plus the API doc comments I changed — `leanCss`, `componentsCss`, `baseCss`, `register`, etc.) with no cache entries. CI generates translations but can't commit them, so the post-merge deploy on `main` failed in ~50s.

My hand-written `hu/guide/cdn.md` didn't help — the drift check wants the cache, not the file.

## The fix

Ran `vp run @pantoken/docs#docs:locales:translate` (the claude-code adapter — `claude` was on PATH) to translate the 9 drifted blocks and refresh the cache + hu pages, then committed:
- `docs/i18n-cache/hu.{guides,api}.json` — new entries, stale keys pruned
- `docs/hu/guide/cdn.md` — regenerated by the pipeline (replaces my stopgap)
- `docs/hu/guide/packages.md` — table-padding re-normalization only, content identical

## Verified
- `check-locale-drift` ✓ and `check-locale-parity` ✓
- The exact deploy command `vp run @pantoken/docs#docs:build` completes clean in ~70s

Once #14 merges, the Deploy docs workflow will re-run on `main` and pass.

One minor note: TypeDoc emits a *warning* (not an error) for the `{@link NESTED_DEPS}` reference in the `register` doc comment (it's a private const). It doesn't fail the build. I left it as-is because editing that doc comment would change its English and re-trigger translation drift — not worth the churn for a warning.

content.text:
Confirmed the root cause. The existing changeset on main (`optimize-ci-release-hooks.md`) has **empty frontmatter** — "tooling only, no release." So PR #13 merged **without bumping any package version**. Nothing new gets published, so `style.lean.css` and `component-icons.css` will never appear on the CDN at the current versions.

**Answer: yes — you need to release, and it's more than css/components.** Everything that gained CDN-facing files or new runtime deps must publish together:

| Package | Why | Current → |
|---|---|---|
| `@pantoken/utils` | New exports (`elevationDeclarations`, …) that css + components now import at runtime | 0.1.0 → minor |
| `@pantoken/css` | New `style.lean.css` export + runtime dep on utils | 0.1.0 → minor |
| `@pantoken/components` | New `component-icons.css` export; foundation relocated | 0.1.1 → minor |
| `@pantoken/web-components` | `register({ only })` + IIFE build; `foundationCss` removed | 0.1.1 → minor |

`utils` is the non-obvious one: the published `@pantoken/css`/`@pantoken/components` import its new builders, so it must ship at a version that has them (changesets pins the `workspace:*` range on publish).

The repo uses changesets, so the release needs a changeset that bumps these four. Let me add it:

git checkout -b chore/release-cdn-distribution 2>&1 | tail -1
cat > .changeset/cdn-distribution.md <<'MSG'
---
"@pantoken/utils": minor
"@pantoken/css": minor
"@pantoken/components": minor
"@pantoken/web-components": minor
---

# CDN distribution: lean token sheet, component-icons, and web-component drop-ins

Publish the files the CDN combine URLs (and the docs picker) point at:

- **`@pantoken/css`** — new `style.lean.css` export: the full sheet minus the
  `--instui-icon-*` glyph set (~22.5 KB gzip vs ~140 KB), the recommended CDN
  foundation. Both sheets now carry the elevation + focus-outline custom
  properties. Adds a runtime dependency on `@pantoken/utils`.
- **`@pantoken/components`** — new `component-icons.css` export (the ~11 icons the
  component sheets reference), so a per-component CDN load resolves its icons
  against the lean sheet. The elevation + focus-outline custom properties are no
  longer defined in `components.css`/`base.css` — they now ship in the token
  sheet, so load a token sheet alongside the component CSS (already required for
  all other tokens). Adds a runtime dependency on `@pantoken/utils`.
- **`@pantoken/web-components`** — `register(target, { only })` registers a subset
  of elements (nested dependencies pulled in automatically); new
  `dist/web-components.iife.js` `<script>` drop-in. The `foundationCss` export and
  its auto-injected `<style>` are removed — the required token sheet now carries
  those custom properties.
- **`@pantoken/utils`** — now owns the elevation + focus-outline declaration
  builders (`elevationDeclarations`, `focusOutlineDeclarations`, `focusOutlineRules`,
  `ELEVATION_NAMES`, `FOCUSABLE_SELECTOR`) so the token sheet can emit them.

content.text:
I've found both root gaps and the extension points. Here's the situation:

**Gap 1 — changesets:** `require-changeset` only runs `changeset status --verbose`, which passes if *any* changeset exists. #13 inherited an unrelated empty tooling changeset, so it passed while bumping nothing. The fix: a coverage check that fails when a changed *publishable* package isn't in the changeset's bump set. The repo already has `scripts/release/workspace-packages.ts` (`isPublishablePackage`, path→package ownership) and `changeset status --output JSON` to build this on.

**Gap 2 — translations:** `check-locale-parity` + `check-locale-drift` only run in the post-merge `docs.yml` deploy — never in PR CI. That's why the drift only surfaced after merge. The fix: run them (or the full `docs:build`) as a PR CI job.

**Hooks:** managed by vite-plus at `.vite-hooks/` (tracked `pre-commit` = `vp staged`, `commit-msg` = commitlint). I can add a tracked `.vite-hooks/pre-push`.

Two policy choices affect daily workflow, so let me confirm before implementing:

questions.question: How should the local pre-push hook behave when a changed publishable package has no covering changeset?

options.label: Warn, don't block (recommended)
options.description: Print a clear warning listing uncovered packages, but let the push proceed. CI still hard-blocks the PR. Keeps WIP pushes to feature branches unblocked while catching the mistake early.

options.label: Block the push
options.description: Fail the push (exit non-zero) until a changeset is added. Strongest local guarantee, but interrupts WIP pushes; can be bypassed with --no-verify.

questions.question: What should the PR CI docs job run to enforce translations?

options.label: Full docs:build (recommended)
options.description: Run the exact deploy command (docs:assets + api-locales via keyless glossary + parity + drift + vitepress build), gated to docs-relevant PRs. ~2-3 min. Guarantees the deploy can't fail — catches drift AND build breakage before merge.

options.label: Checks only (parity + drift)
options.description: Generate EN/hu API pages then run parity + drift, skipping the vitepress build. Faster (~1 min), enforces translations, but won't catch a broken page/component that only fails at build time.

input.new_string:
commitlint:
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true
      - name: Lint PR commit messages
        run: vp exec commitlint --from "${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}" --to "${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}" --verbose

  # Only run the (heavier) docs build when a PR touches something the site renders.
  docs-changes:
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      docs: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.docs }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: Detect docs-relevant changes
        id: filter
        uses: dorny/paths-filter@v4
        with:
          filters: |
            docs:
              - 'docs/**'
              - 'packages/**'
              - 'formats/**'
              - 'platforms/**'
              - 'renderers/**'
              - 'plugins/**'
              - 'design/**'
              - 'pnpm-lock.yaml'
              - 'pnpm-workspace.yaml'

  # Run the exact deploy command on PRs so a broken build OR an out-of-date translation cache
  # (check-locale-drift) blocks the PR, instead of only surfacing in the post-merge Deploy docs run.
  # A guide/API-comment edit that isn't re-translated (its hu cache entry missing) fails here.
  docs:
    needs: [build, docs-changes]
    if: needs.docs-changes.outputs.docs == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true
      - name: Restore vp task cache
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
        with:
          path: ${{ env.VP_TASK_CACHE }}
          key: ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-${{ github.sha }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Materialize generated output
        run: vp run -r build
      - name: Build docs (locale parity + drift + VitePress build)
        run: vp run @pantoken/docs#docs:build

## 1. Changesets — coverage, not just presence

`require-changeset` ran `changeset status`, which passes as long as *any* changeset exists. #13 inherited an unrelated empty changeset, so it passed while bumping nothing.

New `scripts/release/check-changeset-coverage.ts` (`release:coverage`) maps a PR's **shipped** file changes to their owning **publishable** packages and fails if a pending changeset won't bump one. - **Deploy docs** (`docs.yml`) downloads that artifact and publishes it directly — no `vp` setup, no rebuild on the deploy path. `workflow_dispatch` still builds fresh as the manual escape hatch.
- Dropped the now-unused `build-output` artifact from CI's build job.
- Aligned the two path filters (CI `docs-changes` ↔ deploy `changes`) so the artifact is uploaded exactly when a deploy will look for it — and widened the deploy filter to all `renderers/**` (it previously only matched `renderers/web-components/`, so e.g. a `renderers/react` API-doc change wouldn't have redeployed).

## How it flows now
- **Docs PR:** CI runs the full `docs:build` (drift + parity + build) as a gate.
- **Docs merge to main:** CI builds once and uploads `docs-site` → Deploy docs downloads + publishes it.
- **Non-docs main push:** CI skips the docs job; deploy skips too (filters agree).
- **Manual dispatch:** builds fresh (unchanged).

One caveat I'll flag honestly: this adds a cross-workflow artifact dependency, and GitHub Actions behavior I can't fully exercise locally. The two safety nets: the filters are kept identical so the artifact is always present when the deploy wants it, and the `workflow_dispatch` fresh-build path remains as a fallback if the download path ever misses. If you'd rather de-risk, I can keep the deploy building fresh and skip this part — but as written it's the simplification you asked for.

Confirmed the standard model. Now I can give you a grounded answer.

## The key finding

Your changesets today are **gate-only, not release-driving.** `cut-release.ts` bumps versions with `bumpp` using versions *you type* (`vp run release -p components@1.2.3`) and never runs `changeset version` — so the `.changeset/*.md` files (and their minor/patch intents) don't actually determine the released version. They accumulate as documentation + the `require-changeset` gate. That's a real disconnect, and it's exactly what the bot fixes.

## Does switching make sense? Yes.

The changesets action ([pnpm guide](https://pnpm.io/using-changesets), [changesets/action](https://blog.openreplay.com/release-workflows-changesets/)) gives you the automation you want and makes changesets do their real job: contributors land changesets → the bot opens/updates a **"Version Packages" PR** (runs `changeset version` → bumps + changelogs) → merging it **publishes to npm with provenance** and cuts GitHub releases. Most of your custom machinery maps onto it:

| Custom flow does… | Bot equivalent |
|---|---|
| dependent expansion (`computeReleaseSet`) | `updateInternalDependencies: patch` (automatic) |
| provenance publish (OIDC) | `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE` + `id-token` (supported) |
| per-package GitHub releases | `createGithubReleases: true` |
| idempotent skip-if-published | `changeset publish` is idempotent |
| prerelease channels | changesets `pre enter/exit` mode |
| per-package `CHANGELOG.md` | the changelog generator (already configured) |

The main behavioral shift: the bot **batches** all pending changesets into one release event, rather than your current on-demand, per-package `release -p pkg@version`. # Adopt the changesets bot for automated releases

## Context

Releases today are manual, and changesets are effectively **gate-only**: `scripts/release/cut-release.ts`
bumps versions with `bumpp` using versions a human types (`vp run release -p components@1.2.3`) and
**never runs `changeset version`** — so the `.changeset/*.md` files (and their minor/patch intent) don't
actually drive the release. They only satisfy the `require-changeset` gate and then pile up. Cutting a
release means running `cut-release.ts` locally (it bumps, writes changelogs, commits, and pushes
per-package `@pantoken/x@vY` tags); the tag push triggers `release.yml`, which publishes with provenance
and cuts GitHub releases.

The goal: **automated releases**. Decisions taken with the user: **full switch** to the standard
changesets GitHub Action, **batched** cadence (all pending changesets release together), and **keep the
aggregated root `CHANGELOG.md`** as a version-time hook.

Outcome: land changesets on `main` → the bot opens/updates a **"Version Packages" PR** (runs
`changeset version` → bumps + per-package changelogs) → merging that PR **publishes to npm (with
provenance) and cuts GitHub releases**. No manual release step. This also fixes the disconnect — the
changeset bump types finally drive the versions.

## Plan

### 1. Replace `release.yml` with a `changesets/action` workflow
Rewrite `.github/workflows/release.yml`:
- Trigger: `push: branches: [main]` (drop the `@pantoken/*@v*` tag trigger).
- Permissions: `contents: write`, `pull-requests: write`, `id-token: write`.
- Steps: checkout (`fetch-depth: 0`) → `setup-node` (registry `https://registry.npmjs.org`) →
  `setup-vp` (install) → **build** (`vp run -r build`, so the publish path has dist) →
  `changesets/action@v1` with:
  - `version: vp run release:version` (changeset version + root changelog — step 3)
  - `publish: vp run release:publish` (`= vpx changeset publish`)
  - `commit`/`title`: `chore: version packages`
  - env: `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}`, `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: "true"`,
    `NPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS: "true"` (avoid `prepublishOnly` re-invoking a nested `vp` — the concern
    `cut-release.ts`'s `ensureNoNestedVpRun` guards; we build explicitly instead).
- The action creates a GitHub release per published package from its changelog (`createGithubReleases`,
  on by default with `publish`). Preserves provenance + GitHub releases from the old flow;
  `changeset publish` is idempotent (skips already-published versions) and bumps dependents via the
  existing `updateInternalDependencies: patch`.

### 2. Retire the manual/tag-based flow
- Delete `scripts/release/{cut-release,plan-package-release,build-release-notes}.ts` and their `.test.ts`
  (all only referenced by the old `release.yml`/tasks — verified no other consumers).
- Remove now-unused root `vite.config.ts` tasks: `release` (cut-release), `release:plan:package`,
  `release:notes:package`, `release:changelog:root:seed`.
- **Keep** (still used): `release:status`, `release:coverage`, `release:version` (repointed, step 3),
  `release:publish` (`vpx changeset publish`), `release:changelog:root`, `release:pre:enter`/`:pre:exit`
  (prerelease stays available via changesets `pre` mode), and the scripts `workspace-packages.ts`,
  `changed-packages.ts`, `check-changeset-coverage.ts`, `check-repository-metadata.ts`,
  `build-root-changelog.ts`.

### 3. Keep the root CHANGELOG as a version hook
`changeset version` writes per-package `CHANGELOG.md` but no root aggregate. Adapt
`scripts/release/build-root-changelog.ts` to derive the just-bumped set from the **working tree** at
version time — the package.json files `changeset version` changed (`git diff`) + each package's new top
`CHANGELOG.md` section — instead of reading `@pantoken/*@v*` git tags (which don't exist yet at version
time, and whose `@v` format is going away). Reuse its existing helpers (`extractVersionSection`,
`parseExistingRootSections`, `stripTopVersionHeading`). Set
`release:version = vpx changeset version && node scripts/release/build-root-changelog.ts --out CHANGELOG.md`
so the action commits the aggregated root changelog into the Version PR with the bumps.

### 4. Exempt the Version PR from the changeset gate
The bot's Version PR bumps every releasing package's `package.json` (a shipped file) and deletes the
changesets — which would make `require-changeset`/`release:coverage` fail (packages "changed" with no
changeset). In `.github/workflows/changeset-check.yml`, skip the `require-changeset` job when
`github.head_ref` starts with `changeset-release/` (the action's branch). The Version PR still runs the
rest of CI (build, test, lint, typecheck, docs, publint, attw), which gates the release.

### 5. One-time repo settings (manual — flag to the user, I can't do these)
- Settings → Actions → General → Workflow permissions: enable **"Allow GitHub Actions to create and
  approve pull requests"** (required for the bot to open the Version PR).
- Confirm the `NPM_TOKEN` secret still exists (reused for publish auth; provenance rides on
  `id-token: write`).

## Files to modify
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` (rewrite), `.github/workflows/changeset-check.yml` (exempt
  `changeset-release/*`).
- `vite.config.ts` (repoint `release:version`; drop obsolete `release:*` tasks).
- `scripts/release/build-root-changelog.ts` (working-tree mode); delete `cut-release.ts`,
  `plan-package-release.ts`, `build-release-notes.ts` (+ tests).

## Verification
- **Local dry-run of versioning:** on a scratch branch, `vpx changeset version && node
  scripts/release/build-root-changelog.ts --out CHANGELOG.md` → confirm the pending
  `cdn-distribution.md` bumps utils/css/components/web-components to `0.2.0`, writes per-package
  changelogs, and aggregates the root `CHANGELOG.md`; `git checkout -- .` to discard. (Do NOT commit —
  this is just validating the hook.)
- **PR CI:** open the change as a PR; confirm the workflows parse and the branch-exemption logic is
  correct (require-changeset still runs on normal branches — the coverage tests already cover the script).
- **After merge to main:** the action opens a "Version Packages" PR — review the bumps/changelogs, then
  merge it and confirm: npm publish with provenance, GitHub releases + `@pantoken/x@0.2.0` tags, and that
  `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/css/style.lean.css` finally resolves.
- **Idempotency:** re-running publish skips versions already on npm.

## Notes / tradeoffs
- **First real release:** the already-pending `.changeset/cdn-distribution.md` becomes the bot's first
  Version PR — merging it publishes the CDN packages (`0.2.0`) and makes the CDN/picker URLs work. The
  empty `optimize-ci-release-hooks.md` releases nothing and clears out.
- **Tag format** changes `@pantoken/x@v0.2.0` → `@pantoken/x@0.2.0` (changeset publish). Old tags remain.
- **Cadence:** per-package on-demand → batched (accepted). Prerelease channels remain possible via
  `changeset pre enter/exit`, just not automated.
- **Scoped release gates** (old flow gated only the release set) → CI runs the full gate on the Version
  PR. Slightly more CI, much less custom code.

input.content:
name: Release

# Automated releases via the changesets action. On push to main:
#  - with pending changesets, it opens/updates a "Version Packages" PR (runs `changeset version` →
#    version bumps + per-package CHANGELOGs);
#  - once that PR merges (no changesets left), it publishes the bumped packages to npm with provenance
#    and cuts a GitHub release per package.
#
# Requires (one-time): repo Settings → Actions → General → Workflow permissions → "Allow GitHub Actions
# to create and approve pull requests" (so the action can open the Version PR), and an `NPM_TOKEN` secret.

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch: # manual re-trigger (e.g. to re-attempt a failed publish; publish is idempotent)

permissions:
  contents: write # commit version bumps, push tags, create releases
  pull-requests: write # open/update the Version Packages PR
  id-token: write # npm provenance (OIDC)

# One release run at a time; never cancel a run mid-publish.
concurrency:
  group: release
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          registry-url: "https://registry.npmjs.org"

      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true

      # Build so `changeset publish` ships real dist. Publish ignores lifecycle scripts (below), so a
      # package's `prepublishOnly` won't re-invoke a nested `vp` (which can fail with os error 22).
      - name: Build all packages
        run: vp run -r build

      - name: Create Version PR or publish
        uses: changesets/action@v1
        with:
          version: vp run release:version
          publish: vp run release:publish
          commit: "chore: version packages"
          title: "chore: version packages"
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
          NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: "true"
          NPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS: "true"
          PNPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS: "true"

But I spotted something you'll want to know before merging — **CI isn't running on #19**:

```
CI              changeset-release/main   action_required   0s
Changeset check changeset-release/main   action_required   0s
```

Both workflow runs are parked in **`action_required`** (0s, not executed), and the PR shows `checks: 0`, state `UNSTABLE`. This is the well-known GitHub rule: a PR opened with the built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` doesn't get its workflows run automatically — they're held for manual approval. So my "the rest of CI gates the Version PR" assumption doesn't hold as-is. (Good news: the coverage-gate exemption is moot here since the job isn't running anyway, and there's no wrong-gate failure.)

Three ways forward:

1. **Just merge #19** — it only bumps versions + changelogs; the actual code already passed full CI on #13–#18. Merging publishes `0.2.0` and makes the CDN/picker URLs resolve. Simplest, low-risk.
2. **Approve the runs** on #19 (Actions tab → the parked runs → "Approve and run") to get CI green first, then merge. One-off per Version PR.
3. **Fix it permanently** for full automation: give the changesets action a **PAT or GitHub App token** instead of `GITHUB_TOKEN`, so every future Version PR triggers CI on its own with no approval step. This is the documented best practice for this exact limitation.

My recommendation: do **#1 now** to ship the CDN release (that's the thing you've been chasing), and if you want hands-off gating on future Version PRs, I can wire up **#3** (a small `release.yml` change to use a `secrets.RELEASE_TOKEN` PAT/App token — you'd create the secret). ## 3 — GitHub App setup (~5 min)

1. **Create the App** (org-owned so it's reusable): your org → Settings → Developer settings → **GitHub Apps → New GitHub App**.
   - Name: e.g. `pantoken-release-bot`.
   - Homepage URL: anything (the repo URL is fine).
   - **Uncheck Webhook** ("Active") — not needed.
   - **Repository permissions**: **Contents → Read and write**, **Pull requests → Read and write**. (Metadata → Read is automatic. Nothing else — no Workflows permission.)
   - "Where can this be installed": **Only on this account**.
   - Create.

2. **Generate a private key**: on the App's page → **Private keys → Generate a private key** (downloads a `.pem`).

3. **Note the App ID** (shown at the top of the App's General page).

4. **Install it**: App → **Install App** → your org → select **Only select repositories → `pantoken`**.

5. **Add the secrets** (repo Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository secret — or org-level if you prefer to reuse):

   - `RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` = the **entire** contents of the `.pem` (including the `-----BEGIN/END-----` lines).

**[PR #22](https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken/pull/22)** fixes it.

## What happened
#19 merged fine — the `0.2.0` bumps are on `main` — but the **publish** step failed. `changeset publish` calls the npm CLI for its registry checks (`npm info @pantoken/css`), and npm 11 hard-errors `EBADDEVENGINES` because the root `package.json` declares `devEngines.packageManager: pnpm` with `onFail: "download"`.       # the changesets, which the check would otherwise trip); skipping the step keeps this required
      # check green there.
      - name: Require a changeset for each changed publishable package
        if: ${{ !startsWith(github.head_ref, 'changeset-release/') }}
        env:
          CHANGESET_BASE: ${{ github.base_ref }}
        run: vp run release:coverage

Happy to — and there's a key distinction hiding in "OIDC provenance" that changes the decision, so let me separate the two concepts first.

## Two different things

**Provenance** = a signed attestation that ties the published tarball to the exact GitHub repo, commit, and workflow run that built it (shows the green "Provenance" badge on npm, verifiable supply-chain origin). It's turned on by `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE=true` + `id-token: write` — both of which we **already have** in the workflow.

**OIDC trusted publishing** = an *authentication* method. Instead of a long-lived `NPM_TOKEN` secret, npm mints a short-lived credential from GitHub's OIDC identity at publish time. Token-free.

The important part: **these are independent.** You get provenance *either way*. A plain `NPM_TOKEN` publish with `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE=true` still produces full provenance. OIDC just removes the stored token.

So the real question is only about **auth**: keep a token, or go token-free. Both give you the provenance badge.

## The three options, concretely

| | **1. OIDC via `npm publish` loop** | **2. Fix the token** | **3. OIDC, drop tags/releases** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Auth | Token-free (OIDC) | `NPM_TOKEN` secret (long-lived) | Token-free (OIDC) |
| Provenance | ✅ | ✅ (already configured) | ✅ |
| Publisher tool | `npm publish` per package (custom loop) | `changeset publish` (unchanged) | `npm publish` per package |
| npm one-time setup | **47 trusted-publisher configs** on npmjs.com | none (secret already exists) | **47 trusted-publisher configs** |
| Git tags per package | I re-add a step | ✅ automatic | ❌ |
| GitHub releases | ❌ (or I hand-roll) | ✅ automatic | ❌ |
| Effort / risk to ship 0.2.0 now | High (new publish script + 47 configs + unproven path) | Low (one-line auth fix, proven flow) | High (47 configs), but simplest OIDC |

## Why the tooling gap forces this shape

`changeset publish` detects a pnpm workspace and shells out to **`pnpm publish`**. pnpm doesn't implement npm's OIDC token exchange yet ([open issue pnpm#9812](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/9812)) — so OIDC + `changeset publish` fails with the exact `E404` we already saw. Only the **npm CLI** does the exchange. That's why any OIDC option means replacing `changeset publish`'s publish step with a `npm publish` loop, which is what costs you the automatic tags + GitHub releases.

## The "47 configs" cost

npm trusted publishing is configured **per package**, in each package's settings on npmjs.com (you enter the repo `thedannywahl/pantoken` and the workflow file `release.yml`). There's no scope-wide setting, and this release touches all 47 packages (4 core + 43 dependents bumped by `updateInternalDependencies`). So OIDC = 47 manual configs before it'll publish; the token needs zero.

## My read

- If the goal is **provenance / supply-chain integrity** → you already have it; **option 2** ships it today with almost no work.
- If the goal is specifically **eliminating the long-lived token** → **option 1** is the real answer, but it's a meaningful rebuild (npm-publish loop + re-added tagging) plus 47 npm configs, and the token-free win is somewhat undercut by pnpm's missing OIDC support (you're stepping outside `changeset publish`).
- A pragmatic middle: **option 2 now** to unblock the stuck `0.2.0` release, then move to **option 1** as a deliberate follow-up once you've configured the trusted publishers — so you're not blocking the CDN release on a 47-package npm setup.

- **OIDC mode:** `npm publish $ACCESS_FLAG` (lines ~375)

# Wire npm (OIDC) publishing into the changesets release flow

## Context

The automated release publishes via `changeset publish`, which detects the pnpm workspace and shells out
to `pnpm publish`. pnpm's OIDC token exchange is broken (returns 404, then silently skips OIDC — pnpm
issues [#9812](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/9812), [#11513](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/11513);
same `E404` we hit). npm's OIDC ("trusted publishing") is the reference implementation and works, but only
through the **npm CLI**. The prior token path also broke (setup-vp mangles the `${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}`
placeholder in the npmrc → unauthenticated → `E404`).

Goal (per the user + the [yankeeinlondon/gha pattern](https://github.com/yankeeinlondon/gha/commit/c54b13615c89b1beb7f0cf840ca4174603b1e393)):
**token-free OIDC publishing**, while keeping changesets for versioning (the Version PR, per-package
CHANGELOGs) and getting git tags + GitHub releases. All 47 `@pantoken/*` packages already exist on npm,
so trusted publishing is viable (it attaches to existing packages).

Key enabler: the changesets action runs whatever `publish` command you give it and **creates the git tags
+ GitHub releases itself** from the command's output — it does not require `changeset publish`. So we let
the npm CLI do the actual `npm publish` and feed the action the expected output.

## Plan

### 1. Publish with the npm CLI, driven by changesets — `scripts/release/publish-npm.ts` (new)
A publish script the changesets action calls (as its `publish` input) that uses `npm publish`, not pnpm:
- Enumerate publishable packages via `loadWorkspacePackages()` + `isPublishablePackage()`
  (`scripts/release/workspace-packages.ts`), in dependency order.
- Idempotency: skip any package whose current `version` is already on npm (`npm view <pkg>@<version>` —
  succeeds now that devEngines is `onFail: warn`); publish the rest.
- For each to-publish package: run `npm publish --provenance --access public` from the package dir. The
  npm CLI (≥ 11.5.1) performs the OIDC token exchange and emits provenance; no token.
- Tell the changesets action what published, in the format it consumes, so it makes the tags + releases:
  - Confirm which our pinned `changesets/action@v1` expects — stdout `New tag: <pkg>@<version>` lines
    (older) vs. a `CHANGESETS_OUTPUT` NDJSON file of `{"type":"git-tag","tag":"…","packageName":"…"}`
    (newer). Emit whichever v1 reads (pin the exact tag/SHA and match its contract). The action then
    pushes tags (`pushGitTags`) and creates a GitHub release per package from its `CHANGELOG.md`
    (`createGithubReleases`).
- Expose as the `release:publish` task in root `vite.config.ts` (replacing `vpx changeset publish`).

### 2. `.github/workflows/release.yml`
- Keep `changesets/action@v1` — it still runs `release:version` (Version PR) and now `release:publish`
  (our npm script). Drop the token: no `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`/`NPM_TOKEN`.
- Before the action: `actions/setup-node` (node **≥ 22.14.0**, `registry-url: https://registry.npmjs.org`)
  → `npm install -g npm@latest` (OIDC needs npm **≥ 11.5.1**; Node 22's bundled npm is too old) →

# Wire npm (OIDC) publishing into the changesets release flow

## Context

The automated release publishes via `changeset publish`, which detects the pnpm workspace and shells out
to `pnpm publish`. pnpm's OIDC token exchange is broken (returns 404, then silently skips OIDC — pnpm
issues [#9812](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/9812), [#11513](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/11513);
same `E404` we hit). npm's OIDC ("trusted publishing") is the reference implementation and works, but only
through the **npm CLI**. The prior token path also broke (setup-vp mangles the `${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}`
placeholder in the npmrc → unauthenticated → `E404`).

Goal (per the user + the [yankeeinlondon/gha pattern](https://github.com/yankeeinlondon/gha/commit/c54b13615c89b1beb7f0cf840ca4174603b1e393)):
**token-free OIDC publishing**, while keeping changesets for versioning (the Version PR, per-package
CHANGELOGs) and getting git tags + GitHub releases. All 47 `@pantoken/*` packages already exist on npm,
so trusted publishing is viable (it attaches to existing packages).

Key enabler (confirmed in `changesets/action@v1` source): the action runs whatever `publish` command you
give it, parses its **stdout** for `New tag: <pkg>@<version>` lines
(`/New tag:\s+(@[^/]+\/[^@]+|[^/]+)@([^\s]+)/`), and — with `createGithubReleases: true` — **creates the
git tags and GitHub releases itself** (release notes from each package's `CHANGELOG.md`). It does not
require `changeset publish`. So we let the npm CLI do `npm publish` and just print the `New tag:` lines.

## Plan

### 1. Publish with the npm CLI, driven by changesets — `scripts/release/publish-npm.ts` (new)
A publish script the changesets action calls (as its `publish` input) that uses `npm publish`, not pnpm:
- Enumerate publishable packages via `loadWorkspacePackages()` + `isPublishablePackage()`
  (`scripts/release/workspace-packages.ts`), in dependency order.
- Idempotency: skip any package whose current `version` is already on npm (`npm view <pkg>@<version>` —
  succeeds now that devEngines is `onFail: warn`); publish the rest.

- `GITHUB_TOKEN` for the action stays as-is for now (Version-PR-CI auto-run is the separate #20 concern).

### 3. Root `vite.config.ts`
