# Wire npm (OIDC) publishing into the changesets release flow

## Context

The automated release publishes via `changeset publish`, which detects the pnpm workspace and shells out
to `pnpm publish`. pnpm's OIDC token exchange is broken (returns 404, then silently skips OIDC — pnpm
issues [#9812](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/9812), [#11513](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/11513);
same `E404` we hit). npm's OIDC ("trusted publishing") is the reference implementation and works, but only
through the **npm CLI**. The prior token path also broke (setup-vp mangles the `${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}`
placeholder in the npmrc → unauthenticated → `E404`).

Goal (per the user + the [yankeeinlondon/gha pattern](https://github.com/yankeeinlondon/gha/commit/c54b13615c89b1beb7f0cf840ca4174603b1e393)):
**token-free OIDC publishing**, while keeping changesets for versioning (the Version PR, per-package
CHANGELOGs) and getting git tags + GitHub releases. All 47 `@pantoken/*` packages already exist on npm,
so trusted publishing is viable (it attaches to existing packages).

Key enabler (confirmed in `changesets/action@v1` source): the action runs whatever `publish` command you
give it, parses its **stdout** for `New tag: <pkg>@<version>` lines
(`/New tag:\s+(@[^/]+\/[^@]+|[^/]+)@([^\s]+)/`), and — with `createGithubReleases: true` — **creates the
git tags and GitHub releases itself** (release notes from each package's `CHANGELOG.md`). It does not
require `changeset publish`. So we let the npm CLI do `npm publish` and just print the `New tag:` lines.

## Plan

### 1. Publish with the npm CLI, driven by changesets — `scripts/release/publish-npm.ts` (new)
A publish script the changesets action calls (as its `publish` input) that uses `npm publish`, not pnpm:
- Enumerate publishable packages via `loadWorkspacePackages()` + `isPublishablePackage()`
  (`scripts/release/workspace-packages.ts`), in dependency order.
- Idempotency: skip any package whose current `version` is already on npm (`npm view <pkg>@<version>` —
  succeeds now that devEngines is `onFail: warn`); publish the rest.
- For each to-publish package: run `npm publish --provenance --access public` from the package dir. The
  npm CLI (≥ 11.5.1) performs the OIDC token exchange and emits provenance; no token.
- After each successful publish, print `New tag: <pkg>@<version>` to stdout. That's all the v1 action
  needs — it then pushes the git tag and creates the GitHub release per package (notes from its
  `CHANGELOG.md`). No tag/release logic in our script.
- Expose as the `release:publish` task in root `vite.config.ts` (replacing `vpx changeset publish`).

### 2. `.github/workflows/release.yml`
- Keep `changesets/action@v1` — it still runs `release:version` (Version PR) and now `release:publish`
  (our npm script), with `createGithubReleases: true` so it makes the tags + releases from the script's
  `New tag:` stdout. Drop the token: no `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`/`NPM_TOKEN`.
- Before the action: `actions/setup-node` (node **≥ 22.14.0**, `registry-url: https://registry.npmjs.org`)
  → `npm install -g npm@latest` (OIDC needs npm **≥ 11.5.1**; Node 22's bundled npm is too old) →
  `vp run -r build` (publish packs built `dist/`).
- Permissions: `id-token: write` (OIDC + provenance), `contents: write` (tags/releases),
  `pull-requests: write` (Version PR). Env: `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: "true"`; drop the ignore-scripts vars
  (prepublishOnly already removed in #23).
- `GITHUB_TOKEN` for the action stays as-is for now (Version-PR-CI auto-run is the separate #20 concern).

### 3. Root `vite.config.ts`
- `release:publish` → `node scripts/release/publish-npm.ts` (was `vpx changeset publish`).
- `release:version` stays `vpx changeset version`.

### 4. Bump every GitHub Action to its latest version (all workflows)
Verified against live GitHub releases on 2026-07-23. Most pins are already current; three are behind.
Keep the repo's floating-major convention (`@v6`, not `@v6.1.0`) — bump only the major where outdated.

**Already current (no change):** `actions/checkout@v7` (v7.0.1), `actions/setup-node@v7` (v7.0.0),
`voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1` (v1.15.0), `changesets/action@v1` (v1.9.0 — still v1, so the `New tag:`
stdout parsing this plan relies on is intact), `dorny/paths-filter@v4` (v4.0.2),
`actions/configure-pages@v6`, `actions/upload-pages-artifact@v5`, `actions/deploy-pages@v5`.

**Bump these:**
- `actions/cache@v4` → **@v6** — `ci.yml` build job (line 41). Also fixes the deprecated Node 20
  runtime warning CI currently emits.
- `actions/cache/restore@v4` → **@v6** — `ci.yml`, 6 occurrences (typecheck, test, lint, publint,
  attw, docs jobs: lines 65, 91, 117, 149, 204, 327).
- `actions/upload-artifact@v4` → **@v7** — `ci.yml` docs job (line 348), uploads `docs-site`.
- `actions/download-artifact@v4` → **@v8** — `docs.yml` build job (line 81), downloads `docs-site`.

Cross-workflow pairing: `ci.yml` uploads `docs-site`, `docs.yml` downloads it by `run-id`. upload@v7
and download@v8 both target the same post-v4 Artifacts backend, so they interoperate — but they must be
bumped **together** in the same change, and the docs deploy must be re-verified end-to-end (below).

## One-time prerequisite (manual — only the user can do this)
Configure a **trusted publisher on each package** at npmjs.com → package → Settings → Trusted Publisher:
publisher = GitHub Actions, repo = `thedannywahl/pantoken`, workflow = `release.yml`. This release bumps
all 47 packages (4 core minor + 43 dependents via `updateInternalDependencies: patch`), so all 47 need it
before OIDC publish will succeed. There is no scope-wide setting; it's per package (check whether the npm
CLI/API can script it — otherwise the web UI, ~47 one-time). Until a package has its trusted publisher,
its `npm publish` 404s — the script logs and continues, so a partial config yields a partial release.

## Verification
- **Dry-run the publish logic locally** (no real publish): run `publish-npm.ts` with a `--dry-run` flag
  that lists which packages it *would* publish (version-not-on-npm check) and prints the tag/output lines,
  without calling `npm publish`. Confirm it selects `@pantoken/{css,components,utils,web-components}@0.2.0`
  + the bumped dependents and skips already-published ones.
- **Coverage/CI gates unaffected**: `scripts/` + `.github/` changes don't trip `release:coverage`; run it
  to confirm. Unit-test the pure parts of `publish-npm.ts` (package selection, output formatting) in
  `scripts/release/publish-npm.test.ts`, matching the existing release-script test pattern.
- **Real publish (after trusted publishers are configured)**: merge → watch the Release run → confirm
  npm shows `0.2.0` with a provenance badge, tags `@pantoken/x@0.2.0` exist, GitHub releases are created,
  and `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/css/style.lean.css` resolves. Re-running is idempotent
  (already-published versions are skipped).
- **Action bumps (`cache`/`upload-artifact`/`download-artifact`)**: on the PR, confirm the CI `docs` job
  (upload@v7) and the post-merge Deploy docs run (download@v8) both succeed — i.e. the `docs-site`
  artifact still round-trips across workflows — and that the `cache@v6` restore no longer logs the Node
  20 deprecation warning.

## Notes / decisions
- **OIDC-only** (no token fallback): simplest, matches the move off tokens. The linked repo forks
  token-vs-OIDC; we can add that later if a token is ever reintroduced.
- **Provenance** comes for free with OIDC npm publish (it was already configured; unaffected).
- The 47-package trusted-publisher setup is the real cost of going token-free; flag it up front. If that's
  too heavy, the alternative is fixing the token auth (write `NPM_TOKEN` into the npmrc pnpm actually
  reads) and keeping `changeset publish` — not covered here since the chosen direction is OIDC.

- name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          registry-url: "https://registry.npmjs.org"

      # OIDC trusted publishing needs npm ≥ 11.5.1; Node 22's bundled npm is older. Upgrade the global npm
      # the publish script shells out to.
      - name: Upgrade npm for OIDC publishing
        run: npm install -g npm@latest

      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true

      # Build so the publish step ships real dist/. prepublishOnly was removed repo-wide (#23), so no
      # package re-invokes a nested `vp` at pack time.
      - name: Build all packages
        run: vp run -r build

      - name: Create Version PR or publish
        uses: changesets/action@v1
        with:
          version: vp run release:version
          publish: vp run release:publish
          commit: "chore: version packages"
          title: "chore: version packages"
          createGithubReleases: true
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: "true"

name: release-oidc-publish
description: How pantoken publishes to npm — npm-CLI OIDC (not pnpm/changeset publish), driven by the changesets action's stdout parsing
metadata:
  type: project
---

Releases are automated by `changesets/action@v1` in `.github/workflows/release.yml`. Publishing does
**not** use `changeset publish` — that shells out to `pnpm publish`, and pnpm's OIDC token exchange is
broken (E404; pnpm #9812/#11513). Instead `release:publish` runs `scripts/release/publish-npm.ts`, which
uses the **npm CLI** (`npm publish --provenance --access public`) per package — npm ≥11.5.1 is the only
working OIDC "trusted publishing" client. Token-free: `id-token: write`, no `NPM_TOKEN`. The workflow does
`npm install -g npm@latest` because Node 22's bundled npm is too old.

Why this works with changesets: `changesets/action@v1` (v1.9.0) runs whatever `publish` command you give
it with `ignoreReturnCode: true`, parses its **stdout** for `New tag: <pkg>@<version>` lines
(`/New tag:\s+(@[^/]+\/[^@]+|[^/]+)@([^\s]+)/`), and with `createGithubReleases: true` pushes each git tag
+ creates each GitHub release (notes from the package's CHANGELOG.md) *before* it looks at the exit code.
So publish-npm.ts prints one `New tag:` per success and exits non-zero if any failed — succeeded packages
still get released, failures still show red, re-runs are idempotent (skips versions already on npm via
`npm view`).

**Manual prerequisite (only the user can do):** each published package needs a trusted publisher on
npmjs.com (package → Settings → Trusted Publisher: GitHub Actions, repo `thedannywahl/pantoken`, workflow
`release.yml`). No scope-wide setting; ~per package. Until configured, that package's `npm publish` 404s.

As of 2026-07-23: `@pantoken/{css,components,utils,web-components}@0.2.0` + bumped dependents are still
UNPUBLISHED (all prior attempts failed on the pnpm-OIDC / token bugs). This OIDC path is the fix, pending
trusted-publisher setup + a release run. See [[cssdoc-system]] and the CDN work (0.2.0 is what makes the
CDN URLs resolve). Related: [[pantoken-architecture]].

The implementation is complete and everything verifiable locally passes. Here's where things stand.

## What changed

**New — npm-CLI OIDC publish**
- [scripts/release/publish-npm.ts](scripts/release/publish-npm.ts) — enumerates publishable packages in dependency order, skips versions already on npm (`npm view`), runs `npm publish --provenance --access public` per package, and prints one `New tag: <pkg>@<version>` line per success. - [scripts/release/publish-npm.test.ts](scripts/release/publish-npm.test.ts) — 6 tests over the pure parts (ordering, private/non-`@pantoken` filtering, cycle guard, plan split, `New tag:` format).

- [vite.config.ts](vite.config.ts:100) — `release:publish` now runs the script instead of `vpx changeset publish`.
- [.github/workflows/release.yml](.github/workflows/release.yml) — added `npm install -g npm@latest`, set `createGithubReleases: true`, dropped `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`/`NPM_TOKEN` and the ignore-scripts env; kept `id-token: write` + `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE`.

content.text: The publish went straight through (no pending changesets), the changesets action even logged **"No NPM_TOKEN found, but OIDC is available - using npm trusted publishing"** — yet every `npm publish` got `ENEEDAUTH`. So OIDC was detected but the actual publish never did the token exchange. The prime suspect is `setup-node`'s `registry-url`, which writes an `_authToken=${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}` line into `.npmrc`; with the token now unset, that empty auth entry makes npm bail with ENEEDAUTH instead of falling through to OIDC. Here are the search results for your query about npm trusted publishing with OIDC, setup-node, registry-url, NODE_AUTH_TOKEN, and ENEEDAUTH errors:

## Key Issue

When registry-url is set in actions/setup-node, it always writes an empty _authToken line to .npmrc, which breaks npm Trusted Publisher (OIDC) flow when no NODE_AUTH_TOKEN secret is configured. npm sees the empty _authToken, assumes auth is configured, and never initiates the OIDC token exchange, failing with ENEEDAUTH or E404.

## Correct Setup for OIDC

To properly set up npm trusted publishing with OIDC:

1. **Don't set NODE_AUTH_TOKEN**: For OIDC, the NODE_AUTH_TOKEN environment variable should not be set at all. An empty string is still a value—npm will attempt to use it rather than falling back to OIDC. Only when this variable is completely unset will npm automatically use OIDC.

2. **Configure permissions**: The publish job needs id-token: write permission and the actions/setup-node step needs to configure the registry URL.

3. **Use recent npm version**: You must install a version of npm which understands the trusted publishing workflow, which is 11.5.1 or later.

4. **Configure on npmjs.com**: Configure Trusted Publisher on npmjs.com.

5. **Include repository field**: package.json must include the repository field, which is required for provenance validation.

content.text: Root cause confirmed — it's a known bug: [actions/setup-node#1551](https://github.com/actions/setup-node/issues/1551). `registry-url` always writes an `_authToken=${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}` line into `.npmrc`; with the token unset, npm treats that empty auth entry as "auth is configured" and never falls back to OIDC → `ENEEDAUTH`. Let me confirm the recommended workaround before changing the workflow:

content.text: That's the fix, and it's a known bug with a confirmed workaround: keep `registry-url` but strip the `_authToken` line after setup-node. input.new_string:
- name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true

      # Two things OIDC "trusted publishing" needs, done after the toolchain is fully set up:
      #  - npm ≥ 11.5.1 (Node 22 bundles an older npm that doesn't know the OIDC flow).
      #  - No `_authToken` line in the npmrc. setup-node's `registry-url` always writes
      #    `//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}`; with the token unset, npm treats that
      #    empty entry as configured auth and fails ENEEDAUTH instead of falling back to OIDC
      #    (actions/setup-node#1551). Strip it so npm does the token exchange.
      - name: Prepare npm for OIDC publishing
        run: |
          npm install -g npm@latest
          npmrc="${NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG:-$HOME/.npmrc}"
          if [ -f "$npmrc" ]; then sed -i '/_authToken/d' "$npmrc"; fi
          echo "using npm $(npm --version)"

      # Build so the publish step ships real dist/. prepublishOnly was removed repo-wide (#23), so no
      # package re-invokes a nested `vp` at pack time.
      - name: Build all packages
        run: vp run -r build

content.text:
## What happened

The Release run on the #24 merge failed. It went **straight to publish** (no pending changesets on main, since the versions were already at 0.2.0), and every one of the 48 `npm publish` calls errored `ENEEDAUTH` — even though the changesets action correctly logged *"OIDC is available - using npm trusted publishing"*.

**Root cause:** [actions/setup-node#1551](https://github.com/actions/setup-node/issues/1551). `setup-node`'s `registry-url` always writes `//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}` into the npmrc. With the token unset (which OIDC requires), npm sees that empty auth entry, thinks auth is configured, and bails with `ENEEDAUTH` instead of falling back to the OIDC token exchange. OIDC was available — npm just never reached for it.

**Fix ([PR #25](https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken/pull/25)):** strip the `_authToken` line from the npmrc after the toolchain is set up (`sed -i '/_authToken/d'`) — the confirmed workaround from that issue — and fold the npm upgrade + a `npm --version` echo into the same step.

## Next step — your call

Merging #25 triggers a fresh Release run that actually attempts the publish with working auth. Publishing 48 packages to npm is outward and hard to undo, so I'm leaving the merge to you rather than triggering it myself. When you merge:

- Watch [the Release workflow](https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken/actions/workflows/release.yml) — the `Prepare npm` step now prints the npm version (should be ≥ 11.5.1), and the publish should show provenance instead of `ENEEDAUTH`.
- It's idempotent: the 20 already-published versions skip, the 48 remaining retry. If any package's trusted publisher is missing, only that one fails (red step) while the rest still ship — re-run to retry.
- Then check that `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/css/style.lean.css` resolves.

If a re-run is cleaner than a merge for you, the workflow also has `workflow_dispatch` — but note it runs the release.yml on `main`, so the fix has to land there first either way.

Sources: [actions/setup-node#1551](https://github.com/actions/setup-node/issues/1551), [npm trusted publishing docs](https://docs.npmjs.com/trusted-publishers/).
while we wait, the workflows trigger release, which builds packages and CI, which builds packages when merged o main.

You're right — that's real duplicated work. On any push to `main`, two workflows run in parallel and each builds every package:

- **CI** builds (the `build` job, replayed by the downstream jobs via the task cache).
- **Release** builds independently (`vp run -r build`) before the changesets action.

And the Release build is wasted in the *common* case: when you merge a feature PR, there are pending changesets, so the action only opens/updates the "Version Packages" PR — which needs no build at all. The build is only genuinely needed on the rarer publish path (when a Version PR merges and there are no changesets left).

The cleanest fix is to stop building in Release except when it's actually publishing: fold the build into the `release:publish` task (`dependsOn: ["build:all"]`) and drop the always-run build step. Then feature-merge pushes skip the build entirely, and Release stays self-contained (no coupling to CI). The alternative — making Release trigger *after* CI via `workflow_run` and reuse CI's cache (like `docs.yml` does) — removes the duplicate even on the publish path, but it delays every release until CI finishes and couples the two.

One caveat on timing: I'd keep this **out of #25**. #25 is the auth fix that has to produce a clean first publish; changing how/when the build runs on that same critical run adds risk. Better as a small follow-up once the publish is confirmed green.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about changesets action, npm OIDC trusted publishing, and ENEEDAUTH errors:

## Overview

npm trusted publishing with OpenID Connect (OIDC) is now generally available. Changesets works with npm's native OIDC when you use 'changeset publish'.

## ENEEDAUTH Error Troubleshooting

If you encounter an "Unable to authenticate" (ENEEDAUTH) error when publishing, first verify that the workflow filename matches exactly what you configured on npmjs.com, including the .yml extension. All fields are case-sensitive and must be exact.

Other important checks include:

- Ensure you're using GitHub-hosted runners, GitLab.com shared runners, or CircleCI cloud, as self-hosted runners are not currently supported.
- For GitHub Actions specifically, check that the id-token: write permission is set in your workflow.
- To publish from GitHub, your package's repository.url field in package.json must exactly match your GitHub repository.

## Changesets Action Architecture Issue

There's a known limitation with the changesets/action itself. To enable OIDC trusted publishing, you need to add id-token: write permission in that workflow and use npm publish with npm version >=11.5, but the action does both creating and publishing, when you only want to run the publish workflow when actually publishing to npm.

## Requirements

Trusted publishing requires npm CLI version 11.5.1 or later and Node version 22.14.0 or higher.

Based on my search results, I found relevant information about the npm CLI's OIDC implementation. Here's what I found:

## Summary of npm CLI OIDC Conditions for Trusted Publisher Publishing

The npm CLI's oidc.js module is designed to handle OpenID Connect token retrieval and exchange for CI environments such as GitHub Actions and GitLab. It retrieves an OIDC token from the CI environment, exchanges it for an npm token, and sets the token in the provided configuration for authentication with the npm registry.

### Environment Variable Conditions

The environment variables `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL` and `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN` are automatically injected into GitHub Actions workflows, but only if the workflow declares `id-token: write` permissions.

The critical requirement is the id-token: write permission, which allows GitHub Actions to generate OIDC tokens.

### Supported CI Environments

The npm CLI detects when it's running in a supported CI environment, currently GitHub Actions and GitLab CI.

### How npm Attempts OIDC Publishing

The npm publish command calls the OIDC utility with the package name, registry, options, and config parameters to attempt OIDC authentication.

### Provenance Configuration

The npm CLI adds "auto" or "default" provenance to publishes that use OIDC within GitHub and GitLab. It does this by checking the OIDC id token payload and checking if the repository's visibility is public or private—if it's public, it applies the equivalent of adding the `--provenance` flag.

The key takeaway is that npm's OIDC implementation requires the `id-token: write` permission in your GitHub Actions workflow, and the npm CLI will automatically detect the `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL` and `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN` environment variables to facilitate the OIDC token exchange when attempting a publish.

The packages **do** exist on npm (css@0.1.0, components@0.1.1, etc.) — so these are version bumps, not first-time publishes. That rules out the initial-publish gap. Combined with everything else confirmed, here's the full picture:

## Diagnosis

Every client-side condition for OIDC is satisfied:
- ✅ npm 12.0.1 (≥ 11.5.1), Node 22.23.1 (≥ 22.22.2)
- ✅ `id-token: write` — the `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_*` vars are present (the changesets log fires on exactly that check) and forward through `vp` to npm
- ✅ no leftover `_authToken`, no stray `.npmrc`, packages exist on npm

npm's OIDC code (`oidc.js`) then does the registry-side **token exchange**: it sends the GitHub ID token to npm and asks for a publish token. If npm's trusted-publisher record doesn't match the token's claims, npm returns nothing and the code silently `return`s — no error, straight to `ENEEDAUTH`. All 48 failed identically, so the mismatch is **systematic and registry-side** — the one thing I can't see from here, and the one thing only you can.

## What to check on npmjs.com (in priority order)

The classic culprit is the **Environment** field:

1. **Environment** — if the trusted publisher has an *Environment* value set, your `release.yml` job **must** declare `environment: <that-name>`. Ours doesn't set one. So either clear the Environment field on npm, or I add `environment:` to the release job. A set-but-unmatched environment fails every package silently — this fits your symptom exactly.
2. **Repository field format** — npm's form usually splits "Organization or user" and "Repository name". If it wants just `pantoken` (repo name) and it's got `thedannywahl/pantoken`, that's a mismatch. You wrote `repo: thedannywahl/pantoken` — worth confirming which field holds what.
3. **Per-package coverage** — trusted publishers are per-package. You verified one failing package; the release bumps 48, so all 48 need their own record. (If only the checked one has it and it still failed, that points back to #1 or #2.)

I've left the workflow correct as-is (npm upgrade + `_authToken` strip are both still necessary — just not sufficient without a matching trusted publisher).

content.text:
Here's the full picture now. The action's `pushTag` does:

```js
const tagName = `${pkg.name}@${pkg.version}`;   // @pantoken/css@0.2.0
await git.pushTag(tagName);                      // git push origin <tag> — no API path here
await createRelease(octokit, { pkg, tagName });  // never runs: pushTag threw first
```

Two gaps on our side:
1. Our script publishes but never runs `git tag`, so there's no local tag to push (normally `changeset publish` creates them). → `src refspec … does not match any`.
2. Our release checkout uses `persist-credentials: false`, so even with a local tag, `git push` has no auth.

That's why 0.2.0 is on npm but has **no tags and no releases**. And because the packages are now published, a plain re-run will *skip* them (npm-view idempotency) — so it won't re-tag 0.2.0 on its own. The fix splits into "repair 0.2.0" and "prevent recurrence," and there's a real fork on how self-healing to make it:

questions.question: How should the publish script handle git tags + GitHub releases going forward?

options.label: Script owns tags+releases (idempotent)
options.description: The script creates the tag and GitHub release itself via `gh` (skip if they already exist), decoupled from the changesets action. Re-running backfills anything missing — so merging + one re-run fixes 0.2.0 automatically and every future release self-heals. More code.

options.label: Minimal: tag-on-publish + persist-credentials
options.description: Script runs `git tag` after each publish; set persist-credentials: true so the action pushes tags + makes releases. Smaller change, but only tags freshly-published packages — 0.2.0 needs a separate manual backfill and partial failures aren't self-healing.

questions.question: Fix 0.2.0's missing tags/releases now, or after the forward-fix lands?

options.label: Backfill 0.2.0 now via gh
options.description: I create the ~48 missing tags + GitHub releases for the already-published versions immediately from here, so this release is whole. (Creates 48 public releases.)

options.label: Let the re-run handle it
options.description: Only meaningful with the idempotent approach: merge the forward-fix and re-run the release, which backfills 0.2.0. Nothing created manually.

options.label: Tags only, skip releases
options.description: Create the git tags for 0.2.0 but not GitHub releases (less outward noise).

**0.2.0 is fully released.** css, components, utils, web-components @ 0.2.0 + dependents are on npm with provenance, and **all 67 tags + GitHub releases were backfilled** (releases went 10 → 77). 1. `vp run` scrubbed the OIDC id-token env vars → npm skipped OIDC → ENEEDAUTH. **Fixed** by invoking the publish script with plain `node` (#27).
2. The changesets action's `pushTag` needed a local tag + persisted creds we don't provide → tags/releases failed. **Fixed** in [PR #28](https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken/pull/28): the script now creates tag + release itself via `gh release create`, idempotently (dual-scheme aware, `--dry-run`/`--releases-only` modes). 7 tests pass; diagnostics from #26 removed.

Merge #28 and every future release self-heals: publish via OIDC, then ensure tag + release.

## One more thing I found — the CDN docs URLs are wrong

jsDelivr serves **raw file paths** and ignores a package's `exports` map. The files live under `dist/`, so:
- ✅ `…/npm/@pantoken/css/dist/style.lean.css` → 200

- **Add `/dist/` to the advertised URLs** (picker + guide) — quick, but exposes the `dist/` path in public URLs.
- **Restructure the packages to ship the CSS at package root** — clean URLs as originally intended, but touches each package's build output, `files`, and `exports`.

result.output:
1	# CDN & distribution
2	
3	pantoken publishes every package to npm, so you can pull tokens, components, and web components straight
4	from a CDN — no build step, no bundler. This page covers the CSS combine URL (with an interactive
5	builder), plus the web-component drop-ins.
6	
7	## The token foundation
8	
9	Every pantoken component reads `--instui-*` custom properties from a token sheet on the page. Two
10	variants ship:
11	
12	- `@pantoken/css/style.lean.css` — the recommended CDN foundation. It carries every token except the
13	  full icon set, so it's about 23 KB gzipped.
14	- `@pantoken/css/style.css` — the full sheet, including all ~1,777 icon glyph tokens
15	  (`--instui-icon-*`). About 140 KB gzipped. Load this if you reference icons broadly via
16	  `var(--instui-icon-*)`.
17	
18	The elevation scale and focus-ring variables ride in both sheets, so shadows and the focus ring work with
19	just the foundation loaded.
20	
21	## Pick your components
22	
23	jsDelivr's combine endpoint pulls the token foundation plus only the component stylesheets you need, in a
24	single request. Check the components you want, and the builder writes the URL:
25	
26	<CdnPicker />
27	
28	Each component file is small — most are around 2 KB. A component that renders icons (`alert`, `checkbox`,
29	and a few others) needs those glyphs, so the builder adds `@pantoken/components/component-icons.css` (about
30	0.5 KB gzipped — the 11 icons the component set uses) whenever you pick the lean sheet. The full sheet
31	already carries them.
32	
33	### Load order and fonts
34	
35	Load the token foundation first, then the optional base reset, then the component files. The combine URL
36	above already orders them for you. Fonts are the one exception: `@pantoken/components/fonts.css` points at
37	font files by relative path, so combine can't rewrite them — load it as its own `<link>`:
38	
39	```html
40	<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/components/fonts.css" />
41	```
42	
43	### Everything at once
44	
45	Check **All components** in the picker to switch it to the barrel, or point at it yourself (about 141 KB
46	gzipped) alongside the token sheet:
47	
48	```html
49	<link
50	  rel="stylesheet"
51	  href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/combine/npm/@pantoken/css/style.css,npm/@pantoken/components/components.css"
52	/>
53	```
54	
55	## Web components
56	
57	`@pantoken/web-components` registers framework-agnostic `<instui-*>` custom elements. They inline their
58	own CSS, but still read tokens from a sheet on the page, so load a token foundation too.
59	
60	### ES modules (recommended)
61	
62	An ESM CDN resolves the package's dependencies for you. This registers every element:
63	
64	```html
65	<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/css/style.css" />
66	<script type="module">
67	  import "https://esm.sh/@pantoken/web-components";
68	</script>
69	```
70	
71	Use the full token sheet (or the lean sheet plus `component-icons.css`) so icon-rendering elements like
72	`<instui-alert>` resolve their glyphs.
73	
74	To register just some elements — and their nested dependencies — import `register` and pass `only`:
75	
76	```html
77	<script type="module">
78	  import { register } from "https://esm.sh/@pantoken/web-components";
79	  // Pulls in date-input and calendar automatically.
80	  register(customElements, { only: ["date-time-input"] });
81	</script>
82	```
83	
84	### A classic script tag
85	
86	For a no-modules drop-in, load the IIFE build. It bundles its dependencies and auto-registers every
87	element on load, exposing a `PantokenWebComponents` global:
88	
89	```html
90	<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/css/style.css" />
91	<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/web-components/dist/web-components.iife.js"></script>
92	```
93	
94	It's larger than the ESM path — it inlines `@pantoken/components` and `@pantoken/icons` — so reach for it
95	only when you can't use modules.
96	
97	## Pinning versions
98	
99	The URLs above — and the ones the picker writes — track the latest release. Pin a major (or exact)
100	version for production — for example `@pantoken/css@0` — so an upgrade never surprises you.
101	
102	## What's not here
103

1	# CDN és terjesztés
2	
3	A pantoken minden csomagot közzétesz az npm-en, így közvetlenül egy CDN-ből lekérheti a tokeneket, komponenseket és webes komponenseket – nincs szükség fordítási lépésre vagy csomagolóra. Ez az oldal a CSS kombinált URL-t (interaktív szerkesztővel) és a webes komponensek csatlakozásait ismerteti.
4	
5	## A token alapja
6	
7	Minden pantoken komponens `--instui-*` egyéni tulajdonságokat olvas az oldalon lévő tokenlapból. Két variáns érkezik:
8	
9	- `@pantoken/css/style.lean.css` — az ajánlott CDN alapja. Minden tokent tartalmaz a teljes ikontárgykészlet kivételével, így körülbelül 23 KB tömörítve.
10	- `@pantoken/css/style.css` — a teljes lap, amely az összes ~1 777 ikonglif tokent tartalmazza (`--instui-icon-*`). Körülbelül 140 KB tömörítve. Töltse be ezt, ha széles körűen hivatkozik az ikonokra az `var(--instui-icon-*)` segítségével.
11	
12	Az emelkedési skála és a fókuszgyűrű változók mindkét lapon megmaradnak, így az árnyékok és a fókuszgyűrű csak az alappal működik.
13	
14	## Válassza ki komponenseit
15	
16	A jsDelivr kombinált végpontja lehívja a token alapját, valamint csak azokat a komponensmodelleket, amelyekre szüksége van, egyetlen kérésben. Jelölje be a kívánt komponenseket, és az szerkesztő kiírja az URL-t:
17

A teljes lap már tartalmazza azokat.
21	
22	### Betöltési sorrend és betűtípusok
23	
24	Először töltse be a token alapját, majd az opcionális alaphelyzetbe állítást, majd a komponensfájlokat. A fenti kombinált URL már rendezte őket az Ön számára. A betűtípusok az egyetlen kivétel: az `@pantoken/components/fonts.css` relatív elérési út szerint mutat a betűtípusfájlokra, így a kombinálás nem tudja őket felülírni — töltse be saját `<link>`:
25	
26	```html
27	<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/components/fonts.css" />
28	```
29	
30	### Minden egyszerre
31	
32	Jelölje be az **All components** (Összes komponens) lehetőséget az választóban, hogy átváltson a hordóra, vagy mutasson rá maga (körülbelül 141 KB tömörítve) a tokenlappal együtt:
33	
34	```html
35	<link
36	  rel="stylesheet"
37	  href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/combine/npm/@pantoken/css/style.css,npm/@pantoken/components/components.css"
38	/>
39	```
40	
41	## Webes komponensek
42	
43	Az `@pantoken/web-components` keretrendszer-agnosztikus `<instui-*>` egyéni elemeket regisztrál. Beépítik saját CSS-üket, de továbbra is tokeneket olvasnak az oldalon lévő lapból, így töltsön be egy token alapot is.
44	
45	### ES modulok (ajánlott)
46	
47	Egy ESM CDN feloldja a csomag függőségeit az Ön számára. Ez regisztrál minden elemet:
48	
49	```html
50	<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/css/style.css" />
51	<script type="module">
52	  import "https://esm.sh/@pantoken/web-components";
53	</script>
54	```
55	
56	Használja a teljes tokenlapot (vagy a karcsú lapot plus `component-icons.css`) így az ikonmegjelenítő elemek, mint az `<instui-alert>` feloldják a glifeket.
57	
58	Csak néhány elem regisztrálásához – és azok beágyazott függőségeit – importálja az `register` és adja át az `only`:
59	
60	```html
61	<script type="module">
62	  import { register } from "https://esm.sh/@pantoken/web-components";
63	  // Pulls in date-input and calendar automatically.
64	  register(customElements, { only: ["date-time-input"] });
65	</script>
66	```
67	
68	### Egy klasszikus parancsfájl-címke
69	
70	Modulok nélküli csatlakozáshoz töltse be az IIFE buildet. Becsomagolja függőségeit és automatikusan regisztrál minden elemet a betöltéskor, kitéve egy `PantokenWebComponents` globális:
71	
72	```html
73	<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/css/style.css" />
74	<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@pantoken/web-components/dist/web-components.iife.js"></script>
75	```
76	
77	Ez nagyobb, mint az ESM útvonal — beágyazza az `@pantoken/components` és `@pantoken/icons` — így csak akkor használja, ha nem tudja modulok használni.
78	
79	## Verziók rögzítése
80	
81	A fenti URL-ek – és amelyeket az választó ír – nyomon követik a legújabb kiadást. Rögzítse a fő (vagy pontos) verziót a gyártáshoz – például `@pantoken/css@0` – így egy frissítés soha nem lepne meg.
82	
83	## Mi nincs itt
84	
85	Nincs `?components=button,badge` lekérdezési paraméter: egyetlen nyilvános CDN sem állít össze egy csomagot a lekérdezési paraméterekből. A kombinált URL a legközelebbi egyenértékű, és az választó kiírja az Ön számára.

Bootstrap it is. Since it's a brand-new package, do the first publish **without** `--provenance` (provenance can only be generated in CI via OIDC — a local publish with that flag fails). Here are the exact steps:

**1. Build the package** (produces `dist/`):
```bash
vp run -F "@pantoken/plugin-theme-custom-media..." build
```

**2. Authenticate to npm** — one-time, interactive:
```bash
npm login
```

**3. Publish the initial version** from the package directory:
```bash
cd plugins/postcss/theme-custom-media && npm publish --access public && cd -
```

**4. Add its trusted publisher** on npmjs.com so every future release uses OIDC (matching the other 47): the package → Settings → Trusted Publisher → GitHub Actions, repo `thedannywahl/pantoken`, workflow `release.yml`.

**5. Clear the red run** — re-trigger the Release workflow:
```bash
gh workflow run release.yml -R thedannywahl/pantoken
```

That run will now find all 68 packages on npm → 0 to publish, 0 releases to create → **green**. From then on it self-heals via OIDC.

A few notes:
- This is the last straggler — the dry-run confirmed it's the **only** package not on npm; everything else (0.2.0 + the 67 releases) is done.
- The `--provenance` omission is only for this one manual bootstrap; CI keeps `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE=true`, so the plugin's *next* version will get provenance like the rest.
- [PR #29](https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken/pull/29) (the CDN `/dist/` fix) is unaffected and still ready to merge.

E404 on a `PUT` for a new scoped package almost always means npm doesn't see you as authorized to create it — i.e., either the `npm login` didn't actually take, or the logged-in account can't publish into the `@pantoken` scope. Since `npm whoami` came back empty earlier, my first suspicion is the login didn't stick in this shell. Let me confirm:


Done — [PR #30](https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken/pull/30) gates the Release build to the publish path.

## What it does
A `Determine release mode` step checks for pending changesets (the same signal the changesets action uses) and only builds when there are none:
- **Feature merge** (carries a changeset) → Version PR path → **build skipped** in Release; CI is the only build. ✅ fixes the frequent redundancy.
- **Version PR merge** (no changesets) → publish path → builds + publishes, as it must.

Why not the originally-planned `dependsOn: build:all`: publish now runs via `node …` (not `vp run`, to preserve the OIDC env), so a vp task dependency wouldn't fire — gating the workflow step is the equivalent that actually works. Verified the detection locally (no changesets → build runs; a `.changeset/*.md` present → build skipped).

Remaining duplicate builds are only on the rare publish push (justified — Release needs its own dist and stays decoupled from CI) and manual no-op re-runs (infrequent).

- **[#29](https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken/pull/29)** — CDN `/dist/` URL fix (docs + picker).
- **[#30](https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken/pull/30)** — this build gate.
